text: I le Aso Gafua, o saienitisi mai le a’oga fa’afoma’i a le Iunivesite o Stanford sa latou fa’ailoa mai le fausaga o se mea faigaluega fou mo le togafitiga o ma’i e mafai ona fa’avasegaina sela (cells) i ona ituaiga: o se chip itiiti e mafai ona gaosia e fa’aaogā ai masini-vaitusi lomitusi masani pe a ma le tasi sene Amelika i le mea e tasi.

eng_text: Each show would also provide recommendations for books that children should look for when they went to their library.

eng_text: John Grant, from WNED Buffalo (Reading Rainbow's home station) said "Reading Rainbow taught kids why to read,... the love of reading — [the show] encouraged kids to pick up a book and to read."

eng_text: The storm, situated about 645 miles (1040 km) west of the Cape Verde islands, is likely to dissipate before threatening any land areas, forecasters say.

eng_text: Fred is the strongest tropical cyclone ever recorded so far south and east in the Atlantic since the advent of satellite imagery, and only the third major hurricane on record east of 35°W.

eng_text: Jonny Reid, co-driver for the A1GP New Zealand team, today made history by driving the fastest over the 48-year-old Auckland Harbour Bridge, New Zealand, legally.

eng_text: Mr Reid managed to drive the New Zealand's A1GP car, Black Beauty at speeds over 160km/h seven times over the bridge.

eng_text: In April this year, a temporary restaining order was issued by Judge Glynn against the facility to enforce the release of those held more than 24 hours after their intake who did not receive a hearing by a court commissioner.

eng_text: The commissioner sets bail, if granted, and formalizes the charges filed by the arresting officer. The charges are then entered into the state's computer system where the case is tracked.

text: O le vala’auga i le fa’amasinoga e fa’ailoga ai le aso mo le aia tatau a lē ua masalomia i se fa’amasinoga vave.
eng_text: The hearing also marks the date for the suspect’s right to a speedy trial.

eng_text: The valves opening allowed a pressure release for the system and oil flowed on a pad to a tank that can hold 55,000 barrels (2.3 million gallons).

eng_text: The capsule will look much like a shooting star going across the sky.

text: Ua valo’ia e saienitisi o le National Hurricane Center le fa’asolosolo malosi o Danielle ma avea ai o se afā i le Aso Lulu
eng_text: Scientists at the National Hurricane Center predict that Danielle will strengthen to a hurricane by Wednesday.

text: A o taumamao le afā mai laufanua, e tumau lava le faigata ona iloiloina a’afiaga e ono i ai le Iunaite Setete po o le Keripiane.
eng_text: As the storm is far from landfall, it remains difficult to assess potential impact to the United States or Caribbean.

text: Na fanau i le laumua o Croatia, Zagreb, na lauiloa Bobek a o taalo mo Partizan Belgrade.
eng_text: Born in the Croatian capital, Zagreb, Bobek gained fame while playing for Partizan Belgrade.

text: Sa ‘auai i le 1945 ma nofo ai seia oo i le 1958.
eng_text: He joined them in 1945 and stayed until 1958.

text: I le taimi o iai i le ‘au, sa ia sikoaina ‘ai e 403 i taaloga e 468.
eng_text: During his time with the team, he scored 403 goals in 468 appearances.

text: E leai lava se isi tagata o le kalapu e sili atu ona tele ana ‘ai ma lona ‘auai i taaloga uma na i lo Bobek.
eng_text: No one else has ever made more appearances or scored more goals for the club than Bobek.

text: I le 1995 sa palotaina ai o ia o le tagata taalo sili ona lelei i le talafa’asolopito o Partizan.
eng_text: In 1995 he was voted the best player in Partizan's history.

text: O le faʻamanatuina na amataina i se faʻaaliga faʻapitoa e le vaega lauiloa a le lalolagi o Cirque du Soleil.
eng_text: The celebrations started with a special show by the world-renowned group Cirque du Soleil.

text: Na sosoʻo ai ma le fa’afiafiaga a le Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra, o le faʻaili Janissary, ma le ‘au pepese o Fatih Erkoç ma Müslüm Gürses.
eng_text: It was followed by the Istanbul State Symphony Orchestra, a Janissary band, and the singers Fatih Erkoç and Müslüm Gürses.

text: Ona tula’i ai lea o Whirling Dervishes e fa’afiafia i le stage.
eng_text: Then Whirling Dervishes took to the stage.

text: O Sezen Aksu o se tama’ita’i lalelei mai Turkey sa fa’afiafia fa’atasi ma le ali’i pese Italia o Alessandro Safina ma le tama’ita’i pese Eleni o Les Alexiou.
eng_text: Turkish diva Sezen Aksu performed with the Italian tenor Alessandro Safina and Greek singer Haris Alexiou.

text: O le taualuga, sa sisiva ai le ‘au siva a Turkey, Afi o Anatolia (Fire of Anatolia) i le latou faʻaaliga o le "Troy".
eng_text: To finish, Turkish dance group Fire of Anatolia performed the show "Troy".

text: O Peter Lenz, o se ali’i ti’eti’e pasika e 13 tausaga le matua, na maliu ina ua lavea i tuuga taavale i le Indianapolis Motor Speedway.
eng_text: Peter Lenz, a 13-year-old motorcycle racer, has died after being involved in a crash at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

text: A o tapena ai mo lana ta’amilosaga, na paʻu Lenz mai lana uila, ma taia ai loa e le uso tauvā ia Xavier Zayat.
eng_text: While on his warm-up lap, Lenz fell off his bike, and was then struck by fellow racer Xavier Zayat.

text: Sa vave ona ‘auai atu ai le ‘aufaigaluega fa’afoma’i e tiute i le malae ma ‘ave o ia i se falema’i o le lotoifale lea na ia maliu mulimuli ane ai.
eng_text: He was immediately attended to by the on-track medical staff and transported to a local hospital where he later died.

text: E le i lavea Zayat i le fa’alavelave.
eng_text: Zayat was unhurt in the accident.

text: E tusa ai ma le tulaga tautupe i le lalolagi atoa, sa fa’aauau pea Zapatero i le fa’apea mai "o le sisitema tautupe o se vaega o le tamaoaiga, e tāua tele.
eng_text: Regarding the global financial situation, Zapatero continued by saying that "the financial system is a part of the economy, a crucial part.

text: Ua atoa le tausaga o feagai ma fa’aletonu tautupe, lea na i ai ona taimi aupito sili ona faigata i masina e lua ua tuana’i, ma oute manatu ua amata ona toe fa’asolosolo manuia le maketi o tupe."
eng_text: We have a year-long financial crisis, which has had its most acute moment in the past two months, and I think now the financial markets are beginning to recover."

text: I le vaiaso ua tuanaʻi, na faʻalauiloa mai ai e le Naked News, o le a matuā faʻaopoopoina lava ta’iala o lana gagana faʻavaomalō i lipoti o tala fou, ma polokalama fou e tolu.
eng_text: Last week, Naked News announced that it would dramatically increase its international language mandate to news reporting, with three new broadcasts.

text: Ua uma ona lipoti atu i le gagana Peretania ma le fa’a-Sapanī, ae ua fa’alauiloa e le fa’alapotopotoga i le lalolagi ia polokalame fa’a-Sipaniolo, Italia, ma polokalame i le gagana Korea, mo televise, ‘upega tafa’ilagi, ma telefoni fe’avea’i.
eng_text: Already reporting in English and Japanese, the global organization is launching Spanish, Italian, and Korean-language programs, for television, the web, and mobile devices.

text: O le mea na laki ai e leai se mea na tupu ia te au, ae na ou vaaia se vaaiga mata’utia, a o taumafai tagata e taei fa’amalama ina ia ō ese ai i fafo.
eng_text: "Luckily nothing happened to me, but I saw a macabre scene, as people tried to break windows in order to get out.

text: Sa tatu'i e tagata tioata i nofoa, ae sa le mafai ona ta’ei fa’amalama.
eng_text: People were hitting the panes with chairs, but the windows were unbreakable.

text: "O se tasi o tioata na i’u lava ina malepe, ma na amata ona latou o i fafo i le fa’amalama," o le tala lea a lē na sao o Franciszek Kowal.
eng_text: One of the panes finally broke, and they started to get out by the window," said survivor Franciszek Kowal.

text: O fetu e susulu mai ai le malamalama ma le vevela ona o le malosi e maua mai pe a tuufaʻatasia hydrogen atoms (poʻo fuse) e fausia ai elemeni mamafa.
eng_text: Stars give off light and heat because of the energy made when hydrogen atoms are merged (or fused) together to form heavier elements.

text: O lo o galulue saienitisi e fausia se masini e mafai ona maua ai le malosi i le ala lava lea e tasi.
eng_text: Scientists are working to create a reactor that can make energy in the same way.

text: Ae peitai, o se fa’afitauli e faigata ona fo’ia ma e tele tausaga e faaalu a o tatou vaai le fausiina o masini (fusion reactors) aogā.
eng_text: This, however, is a very hard problem to solve and will take many years before we see useful fusion reactors built.

text: O le nila uʻamea e opeopea i luga o le vai ona o le feteʻenaʻi o le laualuga.
eng_text: The steel needle floats on top of the water because of surface tension.

text: O le feteʻenaʻi o le laualuga e tupu aua o molecules i le pito i luga o le vai e sili atu ona tosina le tasi i le isi nai lo le tosina i molecules o le ea i o latou luga.
eng_text: Surface tension happens because the water molecules at the surface of the water are strongly attracted to each other more than they are to the air molecules above them.

text: O molecules o le vai e lē mafai ona vaaia i le laualuga lea e mafai ai ona opeopea mea e pei o le nila.
eng_text: The water molecules make an invisible skin on the water’s surface that allows things like the needle to float on top of the water.

text: O le itu ma’ai o seevae fa’asee i le aisa faʻaonapo nei e lua pito ma le ‘omo i le va. O pito e lua e mafai ai ona mau lelei i le aisa, tusa pe femigoia’i.
eng_text: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: Talu ai o le pito i lalo o le itu ma’ai e lo’u la’ititi, a lilifa i le tasi itu po o le isi, o le itu fa’atautau lea e fesoota’i ma le aisa e pi’opi’o foi .
eng_text: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: O le mea lea e afua ai ona liliu le tagata fa’asee. Afai e liliu seevae fa’asee i le itu taumatau, e liliu foi le tagata fa’asee i le itu taumatau, a liliu i le itu tauagavale, e liliu foi le tagata faaseʻe i le itu agavale.
eng_text: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Ina ia toe foi i le tulaga o lo latou malosi mai le amataga, e tatau ona latou ave’esea le malosi fa’aopoopo latou te maua mai le malamalama.
eng_text: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: Latou te faia lenei mea i le ‘ave’eseina o sina mea itiiti o le malamalama e taʻua o le "photon".
eng_text: They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a "photon".

text: Ua ta'ua e saienitisi lenei gaioiga o le “faaosofia le ‘ave’eseina o le malosi’aga" aua o le atoma e si’itia lona tulaga pe a suluia e le malamalama, lea e mafua ai le ‘ave’esea o le ata o le malamalama, ae o le malamalama o se ituaiga o radiation.
eng_text: Scientists call this process "stimulated emission of radiation" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation.

text: O le ata e sosoʻo mai o lo o faʻaalia ai le ‘ave’eseina e atoma o photons. O le mea moni, e sili atu le laiti o photons na i lō ata (contents) o le ata (picture).
eng_text: The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture.

text: O photons e silisili ona laiti nai lō o mea e fai ai atoma!
eng_text: Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!

text: Ina ua mavae le fiaselau o itulā o le galuega sa fai, o uaea i totonu o le matāuila na i’u lava ina mu ma lē toe ola ai le matāuila.
eng_text: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works.

text: E mana’omia le suia o le matāuila. E tatau ona fa’aeteete i le suiina o matauila.
eng_text: The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb.

text: Muamua, e tatau ona tapē le ki o le molī pe se’i foi le uaea.
eng_text: First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected.

text: O le mafua’aga ona o le eletise i totonu o le soketi lea e nofo ai le vaega ‘iila o le matāuila e te ono sipaka ai pe afai e te tago atu i totonu o le soketi po o le vaega u’amea o le matāuila a o lo o iai pea lesi itu i totonu o le soketi.
eng_text: This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.

text: O le vaega autū o alatoto o le tino o le fatu, lea e pamuina le toto.
eng_text: The major organ of the circulatory system is the heart, which pumps the blood.

text: E alu ‘ese le toto mai le fatu i tupi (tubes) ua ta'ua o alatoto ma toe foi mai i le fatu i tupi ua ta’ua o neura. O tupi aupito laiti e ta'ua o alatoto ninii.
eng_text: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

text: O nifo o le triceratops e mafai ona lamupalaina ai e le gata i lau o laau ae e oo lava i lālā laau malolosi ma aa.
eng_text: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots.

text: O nisi o saienitisi sa manatu na ‘ai e Triceratops laupama, o se ituaiga o laau sa taatele i le faitau miliona tausaga ua mavae (Cretaceous).
eng_text: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

text: O nei laau e pei o ni tama’i niu ma o latou pulou ma’ai, ma lau matuituia.
eng_text: These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves.

text: E mafai e le Triceratops ona fa’aaogāina lona gutu malosi e saei ai laulaau a o le i 'aia le ogalaau.
eng_text: A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk.

text: Na finau isi saienitisi o nei laʻau e o’ona tele, ailoga na mafai e se tainosoa (dinosaur) ona ‘aia, e ui lava o aso nei ua mafai e le sloth ma isi meaola e pei o le koke (tupuʻaga o le tainasoa) ona ‘aai i laulaau po o fualaau ‘aina o’ona.
eng_text: Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.

text: E fa’apefea ona toso a'u e le kalave (gravity) o Io? Afai e te tu i luga o le lau’ele’ele o Io, o le a itiiti lou mamafa nai lo lou mamafa i le Lalolagi.
eng_text: How would Io's gravity pull on me? If you stood on the surface of Io, you would weigh less than you do on Earth.

text: O se tagata e 200 pauna (90kg) lona mamafa i le Lalolagi o le a 36 pauna (16 kg) lona mamafa i luga o Io. O le mea lea o le kalave o Io, e tosoina oe fa’alaititi.
eng_text: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: E leai se vaega malō o le La e pei o le Lalolagi e mafai ona e tu ai. O le La atoa e faia mai i kasa, afi, ma kasa vevela.
eng_text: The Sun doesn't have a crust like the Earth that you can stand on. The whole Sun is made out of gases, fire, and plasma.

text: E fa’aitiitia le manifi o le kasa pe a e alu mamao ese mai le ogatotonu o le La.
eng_text: The gas becomes thinner as you go farther from the center of the Sun.

text: O le vaega i fafo tatou te vaai i ai pe a tatou tilotilo i le La e ta'ua o le malamalama lapotopoto, o lona uiga o le "polo o le malamalama".
eng_text: The outer-part we see when we look at the Sun is called the photosphere, which means "ball of light".

text: Pe tusa o le tolu afe tausaga mulimuli ane, i le 1610, na faʻaaogā ai e le ali’i su’esu’e i le vateatea mai Italia o Galileo Galilei se meavaai fetū e mata’ituina ai o Venusi e iai ona vaega ‘ese’ese, e pei o le masina.
eng_text: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: E maua vaega ona naʻo le itu o Venus (poʻo le Masina) e faʻasaga i le La e malamalamaina. O vaega ‘ese’ese o Venusi o lo o lagolagoina le talitonuga a Copernicus e fa’apea, o paneta e taamilomilo i le La.
eng_text: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Ma, i ni nai tausaga mulimuli ane i le 1639, sa matauina ai e se tagata su’esu’e o le vateatea i Egelani o Jeremiah Horrocks se femalaga’iga i Venusi.
eng_text: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

text: Na umi se vaitau o le filemu na o'o i ai Egelani ina ua mae’a ona toe a’ea o Danelaw.
eng_text: England had experienced a long period of peace after the reconquest of the Danelaw.

text: Ae peita'i i le 991, na fesaga’i ai Ethelred ma se fuava'a Viking e sili ona tele talu mai le fuava'a o Guthrum i le senituri na se’i mavae atu.
eng_text: However in 991 Ethelred was faced with a Viking fleet larger than any since Guthrum's a century earlier.

text: O lenei fuāva'a sa ta'ita'ina e Olaf Trygvasson, se alii Noauei sa fuafua na te toe fāoa lona malo mai le pule a Denmark.
eng_text: This fleet was led by Olaf Trygvasson, a Norwegian with ambitions to reclaim his country from Danish domination.

text: I le mae'a o le tulaga fa'afitauli muamua a le militeli, na mafai ona ioe Ethelred i 'aia'iga ma Olaf, lea sa toe foi i Noauei e taumafai ia maua lona malo i se i’uga lelei e filogia.
eng_text: After initial military setbacks, Ethelred was able to agree to terms with Olaf, who returned to Norway to try to gain his kingdom with mixed success.

text: O Hangeul e na o le pau lea o le alafapeta sa ulua’i faia mo le fa’amoemoe e fa’aaogā i aso uma.O alafapeta na ulua’i gaosia i le 1444 i le taimi o le nofoaiga a le Tupu o Sejong (1418 – 1450).
eng_text: Hangeul is the only purposely invented alphabet in popular daily use. The alphabet was invented in 1444 during the reign of King Sejong (1418 – 1450).

text: O Sejong o le tupu lona fa lea o le Joseon Dynasty ma o se tasi sa sili ona faʻaaloaloina tele.
eng_text: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and is one of the most highly regarded.

text: Sa ia mua’i fa’aigoaina le alafapeta Hangeul i le Hunmin Jeongeum, o lona uiga "o leo sa'o mo le fa’atonuina o tagata".
eng_text: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: E tele tusitusiga i auala na afua ai le Sanskrit. O se tasi o tala e fa’atatau i se malaga mai sisifo o tagata Ariana (Aryan) e aga’i i totonu o Initia na omai ma aumai la latou gagana.
eng_text: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

text: O Sanskrit o se gagana anamuā ma e faʻatusatusaina i le gagana Latina sa tautatala ai tagata i Europa.
eng_text: Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe.

text: O le uluaʻi tusi lauiloa i le lalolagi na tusia i le gagana Sanskrit. Ina ua maeʻa le tuʻufaʻatasia o Upanishads, na faʻasolo ina mou malie atu Sanskrit ona o le tulaga o nofoa’iga.
eng_text: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: O le gagana Sanskrit o se gagana faigatā ma le mau’oa, lea ua avea ma punāvai mo le tele o gagana Initia fa’aona po nei, e pei lava o le fa’a-Latina, le amataga o gagana Europa pei o le faa-Farani ma le Sipaniolo.
eng_text: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: I le taua mo Farani, na amata sauniuniga a Siamani e osofaʻia le motu o Peretania.
eng_text: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: Sa faia e Siamani igoa fa’apolokalama o le osofa’iga o le "Operation Sealion". O le tele o au’upega mamafa ma sapalai a fitafita a Peretania sa leiloloa ina ua o ‘ese mai Dunkirk, o lea sa le’i iai se malosi i le vaega’au.
eng_text: Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak.

text: Ae o le Royal Navy sa sili atu le malosi nai lo le Navy a Siamani ("Kriegsmarine") ma ono mafai ona faʻatama’ia so o se vaatau osofaʻi e uia ālavaa o Egelanl (English Channel).
eng_text: But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel.

text: Ae peita’i, e toaitiiti lava ni vaa Tau a le Navy o le Royal sa tiute i ogāsami e masalomia e iai osofa’iga a o fefefe kapeteni i mea ane gogoto latou vaa i osofa’iga mai le ea a Siamani.
eng_text: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: Tatou amata i se faʻamatalaga e uiga i fuafuaga a Italia. O Italia sa avea ma "uso la’ititi" autū o Siamani ma Iapani.
eng_text: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: O lana vaega’au ma le navy e vaivai, e ui lava fa’atoa uma ona fauina latou vaa fou e fa a o le i amataina le taua.
eng_text: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: O sini autu o Italia o atunuu o Aferika. Ina ia ave fa’amalosia ia atunuu, latou te mana’omia le iai o se nofoaga e fa’amautū iai fitafita ia mafai ai e le ‘autau ona folau mai lesi itu i le isi o le Sami Metitirani ma osofa’ia ai Aferika.
eng_text: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: Ona o lea fuafuaga, e tatau ona latou ave’esea nofoaga autu ma vaa o Peretania mai i Aikupito. ‘Ese mai ia gaioioga, o vaatau a Italia sa lē tatau ona faia se isi lava mea.
eng_text: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: I le taimi nei mo Iapani. O Iapani o se atunuu motu, pei foi o Peretania.
eng_text: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: O vaa moulu na fausiaina e malaga i lalo o le sami, ma nofo ai i lalo mo se taimi umi.
eng_text: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: Sa faʻaaogāina vaa moulu i le Taua Muamua ma le Taua lona Lua a le Lalolagi. I taimi na o le matuā telegese lava ma le fa’atapulaaina o le fana mamao.
eng_text: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: I le amataga o le taua na tele lava ina latou faimalaga i luga o le sami, ae ina ua amata ona atiaʻe meavaai mamao ma sili atu ona saʻo na fa’amalosia ai le folau fa’alilolilo i lalo o le sami.
eng_text: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: O vaaa moulu a Siamani na taʻua o U-Boats. Sa lelei tele le ‘au Siamani i folauga ma le faʻatonutonuina o a latou vaa moulu.
eng_text: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: Ona o lo latou tomai i le fa’atonutonuina o vaa moulu, ina ua uma le taua sa lē talitonuina ai tagata Siamani e faia ni vaa se tele.
eng_text: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Ioe! King Tutankhamun, o nisi taimi e taʻua o "King Tut" poʻo le "The Boy King", o se tasi o tupu lauiloa o Aikupito anamua i ona po nei.
eng_text: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: O le mea e mataʻina ai, e le i tāua o ia i aso anamua ma e le i tusia foʻi i le tele o lisi o tupu anamua.
eng_text: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Peita’i, o le mauaina ai o lona tuugamau i le 1922 na avea ai o ia ma tagata lauiloa. E ui o le tele o tuʻugamau o aso ua tuanaʻi na gaoia, o lenei tuʻugamau na toeititi lava a lē faʻaleagaina.
eng_text: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: O le tele o meatotino na tanu fa’atasi ma Tutankhamun na faʻasaoina lelei, e aofia ai le fia afe o ‘oloa taulima na faia mai uʻamea tāua ma maatāua e seāseā vaaia.
eng_text: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: O le gaosiga o pa’u uili na avea ma mea e māmā ai, televave, ma sauniuni lelei ai kariota a Asuria e fa’ato’ilaloina fitafita ma isi kariota.
eng_text: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: O ū fanafana mai a latou aū maama’ai e mafai ona ati i ofutau o fitafita fa’asagatau mai. E tusa o le 1000 B.C., na faʻalauiloa ai e Asuria tagata ti’eti’e solofanua muamua.
eng_text: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: O le 'au tiʻetiʻe solofanua o se 'autau e tau i luga o solofanua. E le i faia lava nofoa e sa’ofai ai, o le mea lea na tau ai le ‘au tiʻetiʻe solofanua a Asuria i patua lē ufiufiina o a latou solofanua.
eng_text: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Matou te iloa le tele o tagata fa’aupufai i Eleni, saienitisi, ma le ‘au tusiata. Masalo o le tagata taʻutaʻua o lenei aganuu o Homer, o le fatusolo tauaso logologoā, o lē na tusiaina masterpiece e lua sili ona lelei i tusitusiga mata’ina fa’a-Eleni: o solo Iliad ma Odyssey.
eng_text: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: O Sophocle ma Aristophanes o lo o avea pea ma ‘au tusi tala fa’atino taʻutaʻua ma o a la tala o lo o i le lisi o tusitusiga mata’ina i le lalolagi o tala fa’atino.
eng_text: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: O le isi tagata lauiloa i Eleni o le ali’i matematika o Pythagoras, e lauiloa tele i ana a’oa’oga i sootaga o itu o tafatolu taumatau.
eng_text: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: O lo o i ai fa’atatau ‘ese’ese mo le aofa’i o tagata tautatala i le gagana Hindi. E masalomia e i le va o le lona lua ma le lona fa o gagana masani e fa’aaogāina i le lalolagi.
eng_text: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: O le numera o tagatanuu e tautatala i le gagana e fesuisuia’i e fuafua lava i le vavalalata po o le leai foi i gagana o le lotoifale e fa’aogāina.
eng_text: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Pe a ma le 340 miliona i le 500 miliona failauga, ma le toatele pe tusa ma le 800 miliona tagata mafai ona malamalama i le gagana.
eng_text: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: O Hindi ma Urdu e tutusa i vaogagana ae ‘ese’ese i tusitusiga; i talanoaga i aso uma, e masani ona malamalama le tasi i le gagana a le isi.
eng_text: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: I le vaitaimi o le seneturi lona 15, o le itu i matū o Estonia sa matua’i aafia i le aganuu a Siamani.
eng_text: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: O nisi o monike Siamani na mananaʻo e faʻalatalata mai le Atua i tagatanuu moni, o lea na latou amatalia ai le gagana Estonia tuusa’o.
eng_text: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: Na faʻavae i luga o le alafapeta Siamani ma le faʻailoga e tasi "Õ/õ" na faʻaopopo.
eng_text: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: Ina ua tuana’i le taimi, e tele upu na nōnō mai le gagana tuufa’atasi a Siamani. O le amataga lea o le a’oa’oga.
eng_text: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: O le tu masani, o le suli i le nofoalii e alu sa'o lava i le militeli pe a mae’a le aoga.
eng_text: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Peita’i, na alu Charles i le iunivesite i le Trinity College, Cambridge i le mea sa ia aʻoaʻoina ai le Anthropology ma le Archaeology, ma le History i se taimi mulimuli ane, maua ai le 2:2 (o le tikeri o le vasega lua maualalo).
eng_text: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: O Charles o le sui muamua o le Aiga Tupu o Peretania na maua le tikeri.
eng_text: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: Europa Turkey (sasaʻe o Thrace po o Rumelia i le Penisula o Balkan) aofia ai le 3% o le atunuʻu.
eng_text: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: O le teritori o Turkey e sili atu i le 1,600 kilomita (1,000 mi) le umi ma le 800 km (500 mi) lautele, ma foliga fa’atafafā.
eng_text: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: O le itu a Turkey, e aofia ai vaituloto, o lo o nofoia le 783,562 sikuea kilomita (300,948 sq mi), lea e iai le 755,688 sikuea kilomita (291,773 sq mi) o lo o i saute sisifo o Asia ma le 23,764 sikuea kilomita (9,174 sq mi) i Europa.
eng_text: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: O lau’ele’ele o Turkey ua avea ai ma atunuu lona 37 i le lalolagi o atunuu pito sili ona tetelē, ma e tusa ma le telē o Metoropoli Farani ma le United Kingdom pe a tuufa’atasi.
eng_text: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: O Turkey e siʻomia e sami i itu e tolu: o le Aegean Sea i sisifo, o le Sami Uliuli i le itu i matū ma le Sami Metitirani i saute.
eng_text: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: O Luxembourg e umi lona tala’aga ae o lona tutoʻatasi na amata mai i le 1839.
eng_text: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: O vaega i aso nei o Peleseuma sa avea ma vaega o Luxembourg i taimi ua tuanaʻi ae sa suia ia Peleseana ina ua maeʻa le Fouvalega a Peleseana i le 1830.
eng_text: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Sa taumafai lava Luxembourg i taimi uma ina ia lē fa’aitu’au lona atunuu peita’i sa nofoia uma i le Taua Muamua a le Lalolagi ma le Taua Lona II e Siamani.
eng_text: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: I le 1957 na avea ai Luxembourg ma sui na faʻavaeina le faʻalapotopotoga ua lauiloa nei o le Iuni a Europa.
eng_text: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: O le Drukgyal Dzong o se 'olo faʻaleagaina ma o se Buddhist monastery i le pito i luga o le Itumalō o Paro (i le Nuu o Phondey).
eng_text: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Faimai o le 1649, na fausia ai e le Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel le 'olo e faʻamanatuina ai lona manumalo faasaga i' au a Tibetan-Mongol.
eng_text: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: I le 1951, o se afi mafua ai na o nisi o toega o le Drukgyal Dzong e tumau ai, pei o le ata o Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.
eng_text: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Ina ua maeʻa le afi, sa fa’asaoina ma puipuia toēga o le 'olo, e avea ma se tasi o mata’aga mata’ina i Bhutan.
eng_text: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: I le vaitaimi o le seneturi lona 18, sa matauina e Cambodia o ia o lo o omia i le va o malō tuaoi malolosi e lua, o Thailand ma Vietnam.
eng_text: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Sa osofa’ia e Thailand Cambodia i le tele o taimi i le seneturi lona 18 ma i le 1772 sa latou fa’atama’iaina ai Phnom Phen.
eng_text: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: I tausaga mulimuli ane o le seneturi lona 18, na osofaʻi ai foʻi e tagata Vietnamese Cambodia.
eng_text: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: O le sefulu-valu pasene o tagata Venesuela e leai ni galuega, ma o le toʻatele o i latou o lo o faigaluega e i galuega e lē lelei le tamaoaiga.
eng_text: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Lua vaetolu o tagata Venesuela o lo o faigaluega e i le vaega o auaunaga, latalata i le kuata e i falegaosimea ma le tasi vaelima e galulue i faʻatoʻaga.
eng_text: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: O se alamanuia taua mo tagata Venesuela o le suauʻu, lea o lo o aisilia ai i oloa fa’atau atu i fafo, e ui lava e tasi pasene o tagata e faigaluega i le suauʻu.
eng_text: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: I le amataga o le tutoʻatasi o le atunuu, o le poto masani o le ‘au fai togalaau o le Singapore Botanic Gardens na fesoasoani e suia le motu i le Taulaga o Togalaau teropika.
eng_text: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: I le 1981, sa avea ai Vanda Miss Joaquim, o se oketi fa’afaileleina, na filifilia e avea ma fugalaau o le atunuu.
eng_text: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: O tausaga taʻitasi uma i se vaitaimi o Oketopa e latalata i le 1.5 miliona manu ‘ai laau e malaga agaʻi i fanua laugatasi i saute, sopoʻia le vaitafe o Mara, mai maupuʻepuʻe i matū mo timuga.
eng_text: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Ma toe foi atu ai i matu ui atu i sisifo, ma toe sopo’ia ai foi le vaitafe o Mara, ina ua mavae timuga i le vaitaimi o Aperila.
eng_text: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: O le itulagi o Seregeti o lo o i ai le Paka Fa’aleatunuu o Seregeti, o le Fa’asao i Vaega o Ngorongoro ma le Fa’asao o le Maswa Game i Tanzania ma le Fa’asao o le Maasai Mara i Kenya.
eng_text: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: O le a’oa’oina o le fa’aogāina o auala o fesoota’iga e mana’omia ai tomai masani ma le malamalama i aganuu, faapea foi ma meafaigaluega ua lelei ona fa’ata’ita’iina i vasega (laupapa fa’asolo o tala, leo ma le teuteuga o ata, fa’amatalaina o tala, ma isi).
eng_text: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: O mamanu fesoota’i e mana’omia ai lou toe iloiloina o ou mafaufauga e uiga i le gaosiga o ala o fa’asalalauga ma a’oa’o e mafaufau i so o se auala e lē fa’atulagaina.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: O mamanu fesoota’i e mana’omia ai le fesoota’i o vaega uma o se galuega fa’atino i le tasi ma le isi, ae tatau foi ona fetaui i se vaega e ‘ese mai ai.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: O itu lē lelei o tioata fetuuna’i (zoom lenses) o le focal complexity ma le tele o elemeni o tioata e manaʻomia ai le ausia o le tele o taulaʻiga uumi (focal lengths) e sili atu nai lo tioata e le mafai ona fetuuna’i (prime lenses).
eng_text: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: Ua fa’asolo ina le toe iai ni fa’afituli o ia mea ona ua mafai e fale e gaosia oloa ona ausia tulaga maualuga i le faia o tioata.
eng_text: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: O le mea lea ua mafai ai e tioata fetuuna’i ona gaosia ata i se tulaga lelei faʻatusatusa i ata mai tioata e lē mafai ona fetuuna’i.
eng_text: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: O le isi itu lē lelei o tioata fetuuna’i o le maualuga o le aperture (le saoasaoa) o tioata e masani ona maualalo.
eng_text: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: O le mea lea e faigata ai ona faʻaaogā tioata taugofie i le vaega e tau leai se malamalama e aunoa ma se molī.
eng_text: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: O se tasi o fa’afīta’uli ta’atele pe a taumafai e liua se ata tifaga i se DVD o le faata i luga.
eng_text: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: O le tele o televise ua fausia ina ia fa'amalie ai le lautele o tagata.
eng_text: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: O le māfua'aga lēna o mea uma o le a e va'aia i le televise o lo'o tipi le le laina i fafo o le pito, i luga, lalo, ma 'autafa.
eng_text: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: Ua faia faapea ina ia mautinoa ua ufitia atoa le fa'amalama i le ata. E ta’u lena o le fa'ata atoa (overscan).
eng_text: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Ae pagā lea, a pu’eina sau DVD, e ono tipi foi ona laina tū pito, ma pe afai e latalata tele i le pito i lalo ni tusitusiga o ’upu, o le a lē mafai ona fa’aalia atoa.
eng_text: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: O maota o tupu i ia ona po i Europa sa fausia i va'aiga sa o'o ane i mafaufauga, na fa'aosofia ai ata o fetaua’iga a toa, o taumafataga fa'atupu, ma tagata faitaua i taimi o le Tupu o Afa.
eng_text: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: E oo lava i le tu i totonu o nofoaga o le afe tausaga ua tuana’i sa faaleagaina, e aumaia lava i le mafaufau leo ma manogi o taua ua leva ona mavae, e toetoe lava a lagona atu le pa’o o vae o solofanua i maa na fola ai le ala, ma le sogitia o le fefe e alu a’e mai lua o saisaitiaga.
eng_text: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: Ae pe fa'avae ea o tatou mafaufauga i mea moni? Aisea na fausia ai maota o tupu i le amataga? Sa fa'apefea ona fuafua o latou ata ma fausia?
eng_text: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: Masani lava i lea vaitaimi, o le Maota o Kirby Muxloe e pei o se 'olo puipui ae le o se maota moni.
eng_text: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Semanū e le mafai ona tetee atu i osofa’iga umi pe ana leai ona fa’amalama tioata lapopo’a ma puipui manifinifi.
eng_text: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: I le vaitau o le 1480, ina ua amataina le fausaga e Lord Hastings, sa matua to’afilemū lava le atunuu ma sa mana’omia ai le puipuiga mai kegi to’aitiiti o le ‘au osofa’i.
eng_text: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: O le paleni o paoa o se sisitema sa anavatauina e malō o Europa e tausisia le pule aoao i setete uma o Europa.
eng_text: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: O le fa’amoemoe ina ia galulue uma malō o Europa ina ia puipuia se atunuu mai le avea ma se malō malosi, ma o lea sa tele ai ina suia e malō o le atunuu a latou faigapa’aga ina ia faatumauina ai le paleni.
eng_text: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: O le Taua Fa’asologa o Sepania na fa’ailogaina ai le taua muamua o lona ‘auga o le fa’atumauina o le paleni o paoa.
eng_text: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: O lenei mea na fa’ailogaina ai se suiga tāua, aua o malosi’aga o Europa o le a le toe i ai se 'alofaga o le avea ma taua faalelotu. O lea la, o le Taua i le Tolusefulu Tausaga o le taua mulimuli lea o le a fa’aigoaina o se taua fa’alelotu.
eng_text: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Na fa’aleagaina le malumalu o Atemi i Efeso ia Iulai 21, 356 BCE, i se gaoioiga na susunuina ai e le ‘au Herostratus.
eng_text: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: E tusa ai ma le tala, na lauiloa o ia ona o ana taumafaiga e le i fa’avaivai ai. Na tigā tagata Efeso, ma faapea mai e le fa’amaumauina lava le igoa o Herostratus.
eng_text: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Sa matauina mulimuli ane e le tusitalafa’asolopito o Eleni o Strabo le igoa, lea ua tatou iloa ai i nei aso. Sa fa’aleagaina le malumalu i le po lava e tasi na fanau ai Alesana le Sili (Alexander the Great).
eng_text: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: O Alesana, a o avea ai ma tupu, na ofo atu e toe fausia le malumalu, ae sa lē taliaina lana ofo. Mulimuli ane, ina ua mavae le maliu o Alesana, sa toe fausia le malumalu i le 323 BCE.
eng_text: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Ia mautinoa e malōlō lelei lou lima a o e oomi sa'o uma ia nota - ia taumafai foi ia aua nei soona faia ni taga taufa’asēsē i ou tamatama’ilima.
eng_text: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: O le auala lenei, o le a lagona ai lou lelavā. Manatua e le mana’omia le oomiina o ki i se malosi’aga tele mo se leo e sili atu e pei o le piano.
eng_text: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: O le accordion, ina ia fa’aleotele tele, e te faʻaaogāina le pelo ma le malosi po o le vave.
eng_text: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: O le fa’aleagaga o le sailiga lea o le fesoota’iga, fa’asinomaga faatasi, po o le iloaina o se mea moni atoatoa, paia, upumoni faa’leagaga, po o le Atua.
eng_text: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: O le tagata faʻatuatua na te sailia se poto masani tuusaʻo, a’oa’oga, po o se malamalamaʻaga i le mea moni paia / le atua po o atua.
eng_text: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: E mulimuli soo i auala patino o le ola, po o fa’atinoga ua fa’amoemoe e fa’afailele ai na malamalama’aga.
eng_text: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: O le fa’aleagaga e mafai ona ave’ese mai isi ituaiga o talitonuga faʻalelotu ma tapua’iga e ala i lona faʻamamafaina o le poto masani tuusa’o o se tulaga ‘ese o le malamalama, aemaise i le toʻafilemū, malamalama’aga, fa’afiafiaina, pe o se uiga fiafia tele.
eng_text: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: O le talitonuga fa’alelotu (Sikhism) o se tapua’iga mai le konetineta o Initia. Na afua mai i le itulagi o Punjab i le seneturi lona 15 mai se aganuu fa’alelotu na vaeluaina i totonu o tu ma aga masani a Iniu.
eng_text: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Ua manatu tagata o le tapuaiga Sikhs o lo latou fa’atuatuaga o se tapua’iga e ‘ese mai le tapua’iga Hinduism e ui ina latou aloa’ia ona a'a ma tu ma agaifanua.
eng_text: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: E ta’u e Sikhs la latou talitonuga o le Gurmat, o le Punjabi mo le "ala o le kuru". O le kuru o se vaega taua o lotu Initia uma ae i le Sikhism na avea ma mea tāua e fausia ai le ‘auga o talitonuga Sikh.
eng_text: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: O le lotu na fa’avaeina i le seneturi lona 15 e Guru Nanak (1469–1539). Na sosoo ai ma le isi toa iva na e au i le tofiga kuru.
eng_text: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Ae peitai, ia Iuni 1956, na tofotofoina folafolaga a Krushchev ina ua i ai fetaua'iga i Polani, lea sa tetee ai tagata faigaluega i le lē lava o meaai ma le tipi o totogi, na suia i se solo tetee tele e fa’asaga i le fa’a-Komunisi.
eng_text: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: E ui lava i le i’uga, na auina atu e Krushchev tane tau e toe fa’afoʻisia tulafono, na ia ave le avanoa i nisi o mana’oga tau tamaoaiga ma malilie e tofia le ali’i lauiloa o Wladyslaw Gomulka e avea ma palemia fou.
eng_text: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: O le Indus Valley Civilisation o se Bronze Age malamalama i le itu i matu sisifo o Initia aofia ai le tele Pakisitani i aso nei ma nisi o itulagi i matū sisifo o Initia ma matu sisifo o Afghanistan.
eng_text: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Na salalau atu i latou i vaega fa’atanoa o le Vaitafe o Indus, o le mea lea e maua ai lona igoa.
eng_text: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: E ui lava o nisi sikola sa fa’apea mai talu ai o le malo na i ai foi i pesini o le vaitafe Sarasvati ua mago, e tatau ona fa’aigoaina o le Indus-Sarasvati Civilisation, ae o nisi na fa’aigoina o le Harappan Civilisation ona o Harappa, o le itu muamua mai itu uma na eli i le 1920s.
eng_text: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: O le natura fa’amiliteli o le malō o Roma e fesoasoani i le atina’e o togafitiga fa’afomai alualu i luma.
eng_text: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Na amata ona fa’afaigaluegaina foma’i e le Ta’ita’i o Aokuso ma na oo lava ina fa’atuina le ulua’i Vaega Fa’afoma’i a Roma mo le fa’aaogāina i le tuana’i ai o taua.
eng_text: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Sa maua e fomaʻi tipitipi le poto i vailaau ‘ese’ese e aofia ai le morphine mai le ave’ese ai o fatu poppy ma le scopolamine mai fatu herbane.
eng_text: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: Sa lelei i latou i le fa’apipi’iina o itu tino fa’apipi’i i gasegase e sefe mai ai ma le fa’aleagaina o tissue o vaega tipiina o le tino faapea foi ma fa’asoloina o le toto ma le fa’asafuaina o alatoto e aveese ai potoi toto.
eng_text: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: I le tele o seneturi, na ta’ita’ia e le malō o Roma le tele o tomai i le vaega fa’afoma’i ma fausia le tele o mea ua tatou iloa i aso nei.
eng_text: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: O le Pureland orikami e iai ona fa’atapulaa lea e na o le tasi le gaugau e mafai ona faia i le taimi, e le fa’atagaina ni gaugau e faigata e pei o le toe suia o le gaugau, ma o gaugau uma e i ai nofoaga sa’o.
eng_text: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: Sa fatuina e Ioane Samita i le vaitau o le 1970 e fesoasoani ai i fa’avaa e leai ni poto masani po o i latou foi e fa’atapulaa o latou tomai tau afi.
eng_text: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: E atina’e e fanau se malamalama’aga i ituaiga ma tulaga masani o lanu ua fai si talavou ma o nei uiga masani fa’ailogalanu ua aafia ai amioga.
eng_text: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Mo se faʻataʻitaʻiga, o tamaiti e faʻailoa mai ma le toatele ituaiga o lo o mafaufau faʻapea e le lelei i le aʻoga latou te le lelei i le aʻoga pe a latou aʻoaʻoina e uiga i le stereotype e fesoʻotaʻi ma a latou ituaiga.
eng_text: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: O le MySpace o le upega tafa’ilagi e lona tolu le lauiloa o lona fa’aaogaina i le Iunaite Setete ma e 54 miliona faila o tagata fa’aaogā o lo’o i ai nei.
eng_text: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Ua to'atele lava ua aga’i i ia uepesite, aemaise i nofoaga o a'oa'oga.
eng_text: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: E i ai 'itu e lelei ai ia upega tafa'ilagi, e aofia ai le mafai ona fa'aitulau ai se vasega e aofia ai talanoaga, ata fa'asolo, 'ata pu'e ma isi vaega taua.
eng_text: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: O lenei itulau e faigofie ona o'o i ai e ala i se tuātusi e tasi o le uepesite, e faigofie ai ona manatua ma faigofie ona ta i totonu mo tamaiti aoga e i ai fa'afitauli i le fa'aogā o laupapa o ki po'o le sipela.
eng_text: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: E mafai ona fa'afaigofie ona faitau ma fa'atele pe la'iti'iti lona lanu e tusa ma le mana’o.
eng_text: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Attention Deficit maʻi "o se neura syndrome o lona faʻauigaina masani o le tafatolu o auga e aofia ai impulsivity, faʻalavelave, ma hyperactivity po o le malosi sili atu".
eng_text: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: E le o se mana’oga fa’apitoa e a’oa’o ai, ae o se fa’aletonu o le a’oa’oina; e "aafia ai le 3 i le 5 pasene o tamaiti uma, pe tusa ma le 2 miliona tamaiti Amerika".
eng_text: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Tamaiti ma ADD e faigata ona taulaʻi atu i mea e pei o galuega a le aʻoga, ae mafai ona latou mafaufau loloto i mea latou te fiafia e fai e pei o le taʻalo i taʻaloga poʻo le matamata ia latou ata e fiafia i ai pe tusia ni fuaiʻupu e aunoa ma ni faʻailoga.
eng_text: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: O nei fanau e ono oo i le tele o fa’afitauli, ona latou te "fiafia i amioga lamatia, fai misa, ma lu’iina le pulega" ina ia mafai ona fa’aosofia lo latou faiai, aua e le mafai ona fa’aosofia o latou faiai e ala i metotia masani.
eng_text: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: O le ADD e aafia ai sootaga ma isi tupulaga aua e le malamalama isi tamaiti pe aisea latou te faia ai le ala latou te faia ai pe aisea foi latou te sipelaina ai i auala latou te faia ai pe ‘ese ai foi lo latou tulaga fa’atagata matutua.
eng_text: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: I le avea ai ma le tomai e maua ai le malamalama ma a’oa’o ai e suia i se auala e pei ona ta'ua i luga a'e o le fua autu lea na maua ai le malamalama e suia.
eng_text: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: O le auala i le mauaina o fa’amatalaga sa ‘ese lava. Ua le toe i ai ni uuna’iga malosi i totonu o le manatuaina e le tagata lava ia, ae o le tomai e toe manatua ai fa’amatalaga na avea ma se mea ua matele ina taulai atu i ai.
eng_text: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: O le mea moni lava, o le Amataga na faia ai se suiga tele i le auala e a’oa’o mai ai ma le fa’asalalauina atu o le malamalama.
eng_text: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: ‘Ese mai primates, o hominids e le o toe fa’aaogāina o latou lima i le i gaioiga po o le tauaveina o le mamafa po o le upe solo i laau.
eng_text: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: O le lima ma le vae o le chimpanzee e tali tutusa i le lapoʻa ma le umi, e atagia mai ai le faʻaaogaina o le lima mo le aveina o le mamafa i le savali i moto.
eng_text: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: O le lima o le tagata e puupuu atu nai lo le vae, ma ponaivi sosoo o tamatama’i lima (phalanges).
eng_text: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: O ponaivi o lima fossil e lua miliona i le tolu miliona tausaga le matua ua fa’aalia ai lenei suiga fa’apitoa o le lima mai gaoioiga i faiga fa’atogafiti.
eng_text: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: O nisi tagata e talitonu o le mauaina o le tele o miti faʻasolosolo e tele ina lava e mafai ai ona lagona le matuā lelavā.
eng_text: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: O le mafua’aga autu mo lenei mea moni, o le taunuuga o miti manino ua fa’ateleina le umi o le taimi i le va o setete o le REM.
eng_text: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: Faʻatasi ai ma nai REMs i le po, o le setete lea e te iloa ai le moe moni ma lou tino e toe malosi ai, e seāseā lava ona avea ma faʻafitauli.
eng_text: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: E tutusa lava le faigata o lenei mea e pei na tatau ona e ala i luga i minute uma e luasefulu pe tolusefulu minute ma matamata i le TV.
eng_text: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: O le aafiaga e fa’alagolago lea i le tele o taumafaiga a lou fa’iai e moemiti manino i po ta’itasi.
eng_text: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: E le’i solo lelei alumaga mo tagata Italia i Aferika i Matu ae le’i mamao lona amata mai. I totonu o le vaiaso talu ona tautino le taua e Italia ia Iuni 10, 1940, ae ‘avea e le Vaega 11 o le Hussar a Peretania le Olo o Capuzzo i Libya.
eng_text: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: I se 'osofa'iga i le itu i sasae o Bardia, na pu’eina ai e Peretania le Enisinia Sili Lona Sefulu o Vaega 'Au a Italia, o General Lastucci.
eng_text: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Ia Iuni 28, na fasiotia ai le ali'i o Marshal Italo Balbo, le Kovana o Libya, o le suli soso'o foi lea o Musolini, i se taufana o masaniga a’o tu lau'ele'ele ifo i Tobruk.
eng_text: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: O le taaloga fa’aonaponei o le tau sapelu (fencing) e taaloina i vaega ‘ese’ese, mai tamaiti o lo o a’oa’oina i se iunivesite i le fa’apolofesa ma tauvaga o le Olimipeka.
eng_text: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: O le taaloga e taaloina i le vaega muamua e tagata e to’alua, o le tagata tau sapelu e to’atasi e taa’alo ma le isi.
eng_text: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: O le taaloga ta polo o se taaloga e fa’aaogā ai e le ‘au taa’alo kalapu e ta ai le polo i pu.
eng_text: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: E sefulu-valu pu e taa’alo ai i taamilosaga masani, ma tagata taa’alo e masani ona amata mai i le pu muamua i luga o le malae taalo ma fa’auma ai i le lona sefulu-valu.
eng_text: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: O le tagata taalo na te taina ni nai ta, po o le suigi o le kalapu, e fa’aatoa ai malō o le malae.
eng_text: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: E faia le taaloga i luga o le mutia, ma o le mutia fa’ataamilo i le pu e moa fa’apupuu ma fa’aigoaina o le meamata.
eng_text: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Masalo o le ituaiga o turisi taatele lea e fesoota’i ai le tele o tagata ma femalagaa’iga: Turisi e tosina i gaioiga fa’afiafia.
eng_text: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: O le taimi lea e o ai tagata i se nofoaga e matuā ‘ese mai i o latou olaga masani o le malōlō ma fiafia mai lea aso i lea aso.
eng_text: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: O matāfaga, paka o mata’aga, ma nofoaga o tolauapiga o nofoaga taatele ia e masani ona asiasi iai turisi e tosina i gaioiga fa’afiafia.
eng_text: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Afai o le ‘auga o le asiasi o se tagata i se nofoaga fa’apitoa o le fia malamalama i tala’aga ma le aganuu lona uiga o le ituaiga turisi lea e ta’ua o le turisi fa’ale-aganuu.
eng_text: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: E ‘ese’ese mata’aga e asiasi iai tagata tafafao maimoa mai, i se atunuu ua latou filifilia po o le taula’i na o se vaega.
eng_text: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Ua vaaia e tagatanuu lenei gaioiga ona latou valaau foi lea mo ni fa’amalosi’au.
eng_text: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: O fitafita na fa’amalosia tulaga aga’i i luma e aofia ai le 1 ma le 3 o fitafita tumau e 200 ali’i a New Hampshire, i lalo o le ta’ita’iga a Colonel John Stark ma James Reed (mulimuli ane na avea i la’ua uma ma pule aoao).
eng_text: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Na avea e ali’i o le vaega a Stark tulaga i autafa o le pa i le fa’ai’uga o le itu i matū o le tulaga o le Colonist.
eng_text: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Ina ua pe le tai ma aliali mai ai se vaega o avanoa i autafa o le Vaitafe o le Mystic aga’i i le itu i matū i sasa’e o le penisula, sa latou fa’anatinati atu ma sosoo le pa i le tama’i pa maa puipui i le fa’asi’usi’uga o le itu i matū i le auvai i luga o se tama’i matafaga.
eng_text: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Na tuu e Gridley po o Stark se laau ma’ai le isi itu pe tusa ma le 100 futu (30m) i luma o le pa ma lana fa’atonuga e ‘aua ne’i fanaina se fana seia pasi tagata masani.
eng_text: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: O le fuafuaga a Amerika sa fa’amoemoe i le fa’alauiloaina o osofa’iga tuufa’atasi mai itu ‘ese’ese e tolu.
eng_text: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: O le ta’ita’i aoao o John Cadwalder o le a ia amataina se osofaiga taufa’amata’u fa’asaga i fitafita a Peretania o lo o leoina Bordentown, ina ia poloka ai so o se ‘autau e fa’amalosia ‘au.
eng_text: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: O le ta’ita’i aoao o James Ewing o le a ia avea fitafita e 700 i le isi itu o le vaitafe i Trenton Ferry, ave fa’amalosi le auala laupapa i luga o le Assunpink Creek ma taofia so o se fitafita a le fili mai le sosola ‘ese.
eng_text: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: O le ‘au osofa’i ‘autū o ali’i e 2,400 o le a kolosiina le vaitafe e iva maila i le itu i matū o Trenton, ma toe vaelua i kulupu e lua, tasi i lalo o le ta’ita’iga a Greene ma le tasi i lalo o Sullivan, ina ia faia ai se osofa’iga ae le i malamalama.
eng_text: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: I le suiga mai le kuata i le afa maila o le tamo’e, o le saosaoa ua leai se taūa tele ma fetaia’iga ma faigata ua avea ma se mea e fa’ataūaina.
eng_text: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Ioe o se tagata tamo’e i le afa maila e sili ona lelei, o se ali’i ua mafai ona tamo’e i totonu o le lua minute, tatau ona ia ‘ausia le saoasaoa talafeagai, ae o le tauivi e tatau ona fa’aleleia i fa’afitauli uma.
eng_text: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: O nisi e tamomo’e solo i laufanua ‘ese’ese o le atunuu i le taimi o le tau malūlū, tuufa’atasi ma toleniga i le fale fa’amalositino mo le vaega i luga o le tino, o le tapenapenga sili mo le vaitau o taaloga tamomo’e.
eng_text: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: O fa’ata’ita’iga lelei o meaai tau soifua malōlōina e le mafai ona fa’atinoina gaioiga maualuluga, ae latou te mafai ona tausia le soifua lelei o tama taa’alo laiti.
eng_text: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: O le fa’atumauina o le paleni lelei o le malosi, o le fa’amasani i aogā o le lava o le vai i le tino, ma malamalama i vaega ‘ese’ese o mea’ai fa’aopoopo e mafai ona fesoasoani i le ‘au taa’alo e fa’aleleia la latou taa’alo ma fa’ateleina lo latou fiafia i le taaloga.
eng_text: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: O tamo’ega i le afa o le mamao o se taaloga e taugofie; ae peita’i, e tele manatu sēsē e faatatau i vaega laiti o meafaigaluega mana’omia ina ia auai ai.
eng_text: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: E mafai ona fa’atau ‘oloa pe a mana’omia, ae o le tele a lē itiiti po o le leai foi sona aogā tele i fa’atinoga.
eng_text: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: O le ‘au taa’alo e manatu e sili atu le ‘oloa e ui lava ina leai sona aogā moni.
eng_text: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: E mafai ona avea le atomu o se tasi o poloka faufale autū o mea uma.
eng_text: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: O se mea faigata o lo o iai, e tusa ai ma se fa’ata’ita’iga faigofie (Bohr model) o le ogatotonu o le nucleus e fa’ataamilo ai electrons, e foliga tutusa lava ma le si’osi’oina e paneta o le la - vaai i le Ata 1.1.
eng_text: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: E lua vaega ninii o le nucleus - neutrons ma protons.
eng_text: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: O protons e positive le charge o le eletise ae o le neutrons e leai se charge. O electrons e negative le charge o le eletise.
eng_text: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Mo le siakiina o le tagata manu’a, e tatau ona e su’esu’ea muamua le nofoaga o le fa’alavelave ina ia mautinoa lou saogalemū.
eng_text: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: E mana’omia lou mātauina o le tulaga o le tagata manu’a a’o e sōsō atu iai ma nisi fa’ailoilo e ono lamatia ai le ola.
eng_text: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: Afai e te lavea i lou taumafai e fesoasoani atu, ua na o na e galue ina ia atili fa’ateleina ai le fa’alavelave.
eng_text: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: O su’esu’ega ua maua ai o mafatiaga, fefe ma le atuatuvale o le loto ua fesoota’iina faiā o tiga ma le lē ato’atoa o le malosi i tagata o lo o mafatia i tigā o gaugatua.
eng_text: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: Na o aafiaga o le atuatuvale o le loto, e lē o mafatiaga ma le fefe na fua iai fono masani a le PA e fa’atulagaina.
eng_text: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: O ē auai i gaioiga masani e mana’omia le tele o le lagolago i le itu o le ave’eseina o mafaufauga sēsē i tigā, e tuu’ese’eseina ai ‘ese’esega o le tigā ogaoga fa’a’umi’umi ma le tigā o le lē lelei o le fa’alogo i tigā mai gaioiga masani.
eng_text: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: O le vaai, po o le mafai ona vaai e fa’alagolago i le vaega o le tino o lo o iloa ai mea po o mata.
eng_text: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: E tele na’uā fausaga ‘ese’ese o mata, amata mai le faigata e fa’alagolago i manaoga o le tino.
eng_text: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: E ‘ese’ese fausaga ‘ese’ese foi mea e gafatia, e faigofie ona ‘apoia i le susulu atu o ituaiga o malamalama (wave lengths) ‘ese’ese ma e lē tutusa le maualuga o le sa’o o le vaai, latou te mana’omia foi fa’agasologa ‘ese’ese ina ia malamalama ai i fa’amatalaga ma numera ‘ese’ese e galue lelei ai.
eng_text: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: O le faitau aofa’i o le aotelega o meaola o se ituaiga fa’apitoa i totonu o se nofoaga ua filifilia.
eng_text: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: A fa’apea e tutusa uma meaola ta’itasi o se ituaiga fa’apitoa i totonu o se aotelega, e ta’ua lea o le ituaiga e tasi (monomorphic).
eng_text: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Afai e iai ni feuisuia’iga o meaola ta’itasi o se ituaiga fa’apitoa o i latou o le ituaiga felanulanua’i (polymorphic).
eng_text: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: O potopotoga o le ami o loi e savavali ma tautuufua foi i vaega ‘ese’ese.
eng_text: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: I le vaega feoa’i solo, o ami o loi e savavali i le po ae e malōlō fa’atasi i le ao.
eng_text: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: E amata ona feoa’i solo loi pe a le lava mea’ai o totoe. O le taimi lea, e fai ai fa’amoega lē tumau a kolone e fesuisuia’i i aso uma.
eng_text: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: O nei feoa’iga fa’aletuāoia po o savaliga e uma pe tusa o le 17 aso.
eng_text: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: O le a le sela? O le upu sela e sau mai le upu Latina “cella”, lona uiga “tama’i potu”, ma na muamua gaosia e le microscopist na mata’ituina le fausaga o le momono laau.
eng_text: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: O le sela o le iunite fa’avae o mea e ola uma, ma o meaola uma e fai mai i sela ta’itasi po o le sili atu foi.
eng_text: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: E faigofie tele ma taūa sela i su’esu’ega o le olaga, o le mea moni, e tele ina fa’aigoa o “poloka e fausia ai le ola”.
eng_text: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: O le Sisitema o Neura e fa’atumauina le mausalī o totoga e fetuutuuna’i ai i nofoaga ‘ese’ese (homeostasis) e ala i fesoota’iga a neura i le tino atoa ina ia fa’atumauina le gasologa o le toto ia ‘aua ne’i fa’alavelaveina.
eng_text: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: O nei fesoota’iga a neura e mafai ona vave tuuina atu i le tino atoa e fesoasoani e puipuia le tino mai i so o se tau fa’amata’u.
eng_text: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: O asiosio latou te osofa’ia se nofoaga itiiti fa’atusa atu i isi afā malolosi, ae latou te fa’aleagaina mea uma i lo latou ala.
eng_text: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: E se’i i luga e asiosio la’au, saei laupapa mai fale, ma lia’i taavale i luga o le lagi. O le lua pasene pito i sili ona leaga o asiosio e uma i le sili atu ma le tolu itula.
eng_text: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: E tolu afā matuā malolosi ma o la matagi e oo atu i le 480 km/hr (133 m/s; 300 mph).
eng_text: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Sa faia e tagata ma fa’aaogāina tioata mo le fa’atetelēina mo le afe ma le afe o tausaga.
eng_text: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Peita’i, o ulua’i meavaai fetū sa’o sa faia i Europa i le vaitaimi mulimuli ane o le 16 seneturi.
eng_text: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: O nei meavaai fetū sa fa’aaogāina tioata e lua tuufa’atasi ina ia fa’alatalata ma fa’alapopo’a ai mea e mamao.
eng_text: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: O le mana’olasi ma le mata’ū e tumau pea ona iai ia i tatou ma o le natura o le galulue fa’atasi, ina ua manuia le to’atele o le a fa’ateleina pea mea e maua i le taimi pupuu e ala i le galue ma le lē manatu i isi.
eng_text: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: Talosia ae malamalama le tele o tagata o le latou filifiliga sili mo le taimi umi o le galulue fa’atasi ma isi.
eng_text: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: O le tele o tagata o lo o moemiti i le aso e mafai ai ona malaga i isi fetū ma su’esu’e ai i isi lalolagi, o nisi tagata e fia iloa po o a mea o iai o isi e talitonu o tagata ‘ese (aliens) po o isi ola masalo e mafai ona ola i luga o se isi laau.
eng_text: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Peita’i, afai e tupu lenei mea masalo e le toe tupu i se taimi umi. Ua ta’ape solo fetū ma ua faitau miliona o maila le va o fetū e “tua’oi”.
