eng_text: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Masalo e iai se aso, o fanau a fanau a lau fanau (great grandchildren) o le a tūtū ai i luga o se lalolagi o tagata ‘ese ma mafaufau fia iloa po o ai lo latou tupu’aga mai anamua.
eng_text: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: O meaola e fai i sela e tele. Latou te aai so o se mea’ai ma fa’amalū i totonu. O le tele o manu e mafai ona gaoioi.
eng_text: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Na o meaola e iai fai’ai (e ui e le o meaola uma; mo le fa’ata’ita’iga, o le jellyfish, e leai se fai’ai).
eng_text: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: O meaola e maua i vaega uma o le lalolagi. Latou te eli le palapala, aau i ogasami, ma felele i le lagi.
eng_text: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: O le sela o le fausaga pito i la’ititi ma o le vaega ola o se mea e ola.
eng_text: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: O le sela e sau mai le ‘upu Latina cella o lona uiga o le potu la’ititi.
eng_text: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: A e vaai i se mea e ola i le microscope, e te iloa ai e fai mai i fa’atafafa po o polo laiti.
eng_text: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: O le ali’i su’esu’e i meaola o Robert Hooke, sa vaaia fa’atafafa laiti i totonu o le momono i le microscope.
eng_text: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: E foliga e pei ni potu. O ia o le tagata muamua na iloaina sela pēpē.
eng_text: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: O elemeni ma compounds e mafai ona feoa’i mai le isi setete i le isi e aunoa ma se suiga.
eng_text: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: O le kasa o le nitrogen e tutusa meatotino ma le nitrogen liquid. O le tulaga i le vai e mafiafia ae o molecules o lo o tumau lava.
eng_text: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: O le vai le isi fa’ata’ita’iga. O le compound water e gaosia mai i atomu o hydrogen e lua ma le tasi atomu o le okesene.
eng_text: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: E tutusa lava fausaga o molecule pe kasa, suavai, pe malō.
eng_text: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: E ui lava ina mafai ona suia lona tulaga fa’aletino (physical state), ae o lona tulaga fa’availaau (chemical state) e tumau lava.
eng_text: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: O le taimi o se mea o lo o si’omia ai i tatou, ma aafia ai mea uma tatou te faia, peita’i e faigata pea ona malamalama iai.
eng_text: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Sa su’esu’eina le taimi e tagata lotu, filosofia, ma sikola o le saienitisi mo le faitau afe o tausaga.
eng_text: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Ua tatou iloa le taimi o se fa’asologa o mea e tutupu mai le lumana’i e ala mai i le taimi nei aga’i le taimi tuana’i.
eng_text: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: O le taimi foi tatou te iloa ai fa’atusatusa le ‘umi (‘umi) o mea e tutupu.
eng_text: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: E mafai ona e makaina le taimi ua te’a e ala i le maitauina o se mea e fa’aauau ona faia mai lea taimi i lea taimi. O le cyclical event o se mea masani e tupu ma toe tupu.
eng_text: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: O komepiuta i ona po nei ua fa’aaogā e suia ata ma vitiō (videos).
eng_text: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: O le tomai maualuga i le fa’agaioina o ata ua mafai ona gaosia i komepiuta, ma o lenei ituaiga o ata tifaga ua fa’atuputupula’ia lona fa’aaogāina i televise ma tifaga.
eng_text: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: O musika e masani ona pu’eina i komepiuta fa’apitoa e suia ma tuufa’atasia ai leo.
eng_text: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Mo se taimi umi i le vaitaimi o le sefulu-iva ma le luasefulu seneturi, e talitonu o tagata muamua sa nofoia Ni’u Sila o le ‘au Maoli, sa latou tuli manu i manulele tetele ua ta’ua o moa.
eng_text: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: O le talitonuga na fa’atuina ai le manatu o tagata Maoli na malaga mai le Polenisia i se Vaa Tele ma ave’esea Ni’u Sila mai Moriori, ma amataina ai se fa’apotopotoga o fai fa’ato’aga.
eng_text: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Peita’i o fa’amaoniga fou ua iloa ai o Moriori o se kulupu o tagata Maoli mai le vaega autū o le atunuu na malaga mai Ni’u Sila aga’i i Motu o Chatham, ma atina’e ai la latou aganuu uiga ‘ese ma le filemu.
eng_text: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Sa iai foi le isi ituaiga i atumotu o Chatham o i latou ia o Maoli na malaga ‘ese mai Ni’u Sila.
eng_text: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Na latou ta’ua i latou lava o Moriori sa iai ni nai taua na tutupu ma i’u ai ina soloiesea tagata Moriori.
eng_text: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: O tagata ta’ito’atasi sa auai i le tele o tausaga na fesoasoani ia i matou e talisapaia lo matou malosi ma matou naunauta’iga a o iloiloina ma le fa’amaoni fa’afitauli e oo lava i to’ilalo.
eng_text: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: A o fa’alogologo i tagata ta’ito’atasi o fa’asoa mai tala o latou aiga ta’itasi, ma tala i fa’alapotopotoga, na matou maua ai se malamalama taūa i mea na tutupu ma nisi o uiga fa’aletagata na maua ai suiga lelei po o le fa’aleagaina o le aganuu o le fa’alapotopotoga.
eng_text: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: O le malamalama i le tala’aga o se tasi e le o le malamalama lea i le aganuu, ae e fesoasoani i tagata ia maua so latou iloa o le vaega latou te iai i le tala fa’asolopito o le fa’apotopotoga.
eng_text: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: A o iloiloina fa’amanuiaga ma amata ona malamalama i le i’uvale, o tagata ta’ito’atasi ma le lautele o tagata auai latou te iloa atili le loloto o le meaaogā, vaaiga taula’i, ma malosi’aga o lo o ūna’ia le fa’alapotopotoga.
eng_text: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: I lenei tulaga, o le manatuaina o amioga fa’afaipisinisi i aso ua mavae ma taunuuga manuia na fesoasoani i tagata e tatala o latou mafaufau i suiga fou ma se ta’ita’iga fou mo le ekalesia o le lotoifale.
eng_text: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: O ia ituaiga tala manuia e fa’aitiitia ai le fefe i suiga, a o fa’atupu ai lagona lelei i suiga i le lumana’i.
eng_text: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: O mafaufauga e 'aumai'a fa'atasi o metotia ia e fofō ai fa'afitauli e tu'ufa'atasi ai manatu ese'ese po'o vala e saili ai se fofō.
eng_text: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: O le taula’iga o lea manatu o le saosaoa, mafua’aga ma le manino, fa’atasi ai ma le fa’asinoina o le mea moni, toe fa’aogaina o fa’atatau metotia o lo’o i ai, ma ao mai fa’amatalaga.
eng_text: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: O le vala ’aupito tāua o lea manatu maumaututū o le: e tasi lava le tali sa’o. E na’o le lua tali e te manatu i ai, e ta’u o le sa’o poo le sese
eng_text: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: O le ituaiga mafaufauga lea e feso'ota'i ma saienisi patino po'o taualumaga i alafua tatau.
eng_text: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: O tagata e i ai lea ’itua’iga mafaufauga lea e fuafua lelei manatu, e mafai ona tauloto fa’agasologa, fōfō fa’afitauli ma galulue i suega fa’asaienisi.
eng_text: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: O tagata o se ituaiga e sili atu le atamai i le faitauina o mafaufau o isi.
eng_text: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: O lona uiga e mafai ona tatou mateina po o a mafaufauga o isi tagata, o latou fa’amoemoega, talitonuga, iloa po o mo’omo’oga.
eng_text: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: I nei tomai uma, o le malamalama i fa’anaunauga o isi e taūa tele. E mafai ai ona tatou fo’ia ni fa’afitauli o gaioiga fa’atino.
eng_text: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Mo le fa’ata’ita’iga, afai e te vaai i se tagata o tata’e le fa’amalama o se taavale, masalo e te mafaufau o lo o taumafai e gaoi le taavale a se tagata ‘ese.
eng_text: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: E tatau ona fa’amasinoina ‘ese o ia pe a fa’apea ua leiloa le ki o lana taavale ma o lana ia taavale na taumafai e talepe.
eng_text: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: O le MRI e faia i luga o gaioiga fa’aletino e vaaia (physics phenomenon) e ta’ua o le nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), lea na fa’ailoaina i le vaitaimi o le 1930 e Felix Bloch (e galue i le Iunivesitē o Stanford) ma Edward Purcell (mai le Iunivesitē o Harvard).
eng_text: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: I lea leo, o vaega maneta ma radio waves e afua ai ona fa’asafua e atomu fa’ailoilo laiti o le leitiō.
eng_text: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: I le tausaga 1970, o Raymon Damadian, o se ali’i foma’i ma se saienitisi su’esu’e na ia mu’ai fa’ailoaina le fa’aaogāina o le fa’ata (magnetic resonance imaging) o se meafaigaluega mo le sa’iliina o ma’i.
eng_text: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: I le fa tausaga mulimuli ane na tuuina mai ai le fa’atagana, na avea ma laisene muamua i le lalolagi i le vaega o le MRI.
eng_text: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: I le 1977, o le ali’i foma’i o Dr. Damadian na fa’aumaina le fausaga o le “tino-atoa” muamua o le fa’ata o le MRI, lea na ia fa’aigoaina o le “Lē to’ilalo”.
eng_text: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: O fesoota’iga i taimi ‘ese’ese (asynchronous) e fa’amalosia le taimi mo le toe manatunatu ma le tali atu i isi.
eng_text: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: E mafai ai e tamaiti a’oga ona galulue i lo latou lava fua fa’atatau ma pulea le fua fa’atatau o fa’amatalaga fa’a-fa’atonuga.
eng_text: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: I se fa’aopoopoga, e laiti taimi fa’atulagaina ma le mafai e fetuutuuna’i ai itulā faigaluega. (Bremer, 1998).
eng_text: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: O le fa’aaogāina o le Initaneti ma le World Wide Web ua mafai ai e tamaiti a’oga ona maua fa’amatalaga i taimi uma.
eng_text: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: E mafai foi e tamaiti ona tuuina atu fesili i faia’oga i so o se taimi o le aso ma fa’atalitali ni tali vave, na i lo le fa’atali seia oo i le isi fono fa’afesaga’i.
eng_text: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: O fa’atalatalanoaga i auala fa’aonaponei i a’oa’oga e saunia ai le sa’olotoga mai tulafono. E leai se isi auala lelei e a’oa’o ai.
eng_text: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: O le mea moni, e lē tasi se mea lelei e a’oa’o. O a’oa’oga e fa’aosofia i le poto masani i le va o le tagata a’oa’o ma le malamalama fa’aalia.
eng_text: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: O le tatou tomai o lo o iai i le faia e oe o mea uma ma le fa’alauiloaina o fa’amatalaga, o a’oga i luga o fa’aaliga i le televise ua fa’ailoaina lea tulaga.
eng_text: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: E to’atele na’uā i tatou e matamata i ata i televise e fa’ailoa mai ai se fa’agasologa po o se tomai tatou te le i auai lava iai po o le fa’aaogā iai o lenā poto masani.
eng_text: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Tatou te le toe suia se taavale, fausia se āfu laititi i o tatou tuāfale, malaga i Perū e su’esu’e mea fa’aleagaina mai anamuā, pe toe fai fa’alelei le fale o le tatou tuā’oi.
eng_text: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Fa’afetai i fiber optic cable i lalo o le sami o lo o fesoota’i i Europa ma satelite broadband, ua lelei sootaga a Greenland e 93% o lona faitau aofa’i ua oo iai le initaneti.
eng_text: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: O ou faletalimalō po o tali malō (pe a nofo i se fale talimalō po o se fale tuma’oti) e mautinoa le iai o le wifi po o le initaneti e fesoota’i i le PC, ma o fale uma e iai ofisa o le initaneti po o isi nofoaga i le wifi mo tagata lautele.
eng_text: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: E pei ona tā’ua i luga, e ui o le upu lea “Eskimo” (Sa’a) e taliaina pea i totonu o le Sitete o Amerika, e i ai le manatu o tagata Aratika, aemaise lava tagata mai Kanata e lē fa’aaloalo lea upu.
eng_text: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Pe a e fa'alogo i le upu o lo’o fa’aaogaina e tagata Greenland, e lē tatau ona fa’aaogaina e tagata mai isi atunu'u.
eng_text: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: O tagatānu'u moni o Greenland e ta’ua i latou o Inuit ma Kalaalleq i totonu o Kanata (numera tele Kalaallit) o le Greenlander, i Greenland.
eng_text: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Solitulafono, ma mea leaga e ai i tagata uma mai isi atunuu, e tau le iloa i Greenland. E oo i taulaga e leai ni “nofoaga fa’aeteetegatā.”
eng_text: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Masalo na o le tau malūlū le taufa’amata’u moni o le a feagai ma le tagata e le i tapena.
eng_text: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Afai e te asiasi i le Greenland i le taimi o le tau malūlū (ia e iloa o le mamao o lau alu i matū, o le malūlū tele foi lena e oo iai), e taūa tele le tapena fa’alava o ofu mafanafana.
eng_text: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: O le uumi o aso i le tau mafanafana e mafai ona oo atu i fa’afitauli o le lē lava o le moe ma isi fa’afitauli o le soifua malōlōina.
eng_text: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: O le tau mafanafana, e tatau foi ona e mataala i namu o atunuu o loo iai i Europa Matu (Nordic) ma Atalani Matu. E ui ina latou le feave’aiina ni fa’ama’i ae fa’alavelave.
eng_text: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: A o fesoota’i atu ai le tamaoaiga o San Francisco ua avea o se mata’aga e maualuga lona tulaga i le lalolagi, o lona tamaoaiga e fa’ateleina.
eng_text: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: O le vaega o tagata faigaluega e sili ona to’atele o ‘au’aunaga fa’apolofesa, o le malō, o tupe, fefa’ataua’iga, ma turisi.
eng_text: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: O lona iloa ai i musika, ata tifaga, tusitusiga ma aganuu ta’uta’ua ua fesoasoani i le faiga o le taulaga ma mata’aga ua lauiloa ai i le lalolagi.
eng_text: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: Ua fausia e San Fransico se atina’e turisi tele e iai le anoanoa’i o faletalimalō, fale’aiga, ma fale fono lelei ona fausia ma maualuga lona tulaga.
eng_text: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: O San Francisco foi o se tasi o nofoaga sili ona lelei i le atunuu mo isi mea’ai Asia: Kolea, Thai, Initia, ma Sapanī.
eng_text: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: O malaga i le Walt Disney World e fai ma fa’ailoga o se malaga tele i le to’atele o aiga Amerika.
eng_text: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: O asiasiga “masani” e aofia ai le lele aga’i i le malae vaalele fa’a-va-o-malō o Orlando, alu i le pasi i le faletalimalō i Disney, fa’aalu ai po o se vaiaso e aunoa ma le tuua o meatotino a le Disney, ma toe fo’i ai i le aiga.
eng_text: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: E iai limiti o suiga talafeagai, peita’i e tumau pea i le tele o tagata pe a talanoa i le “alu i le Disney World.”
eng_text: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: O le tele o ticket e fa’atau i luga o ‘upega tafa’ilagi i uepesite fa’atau tu’i e pei o le eBay po o le Craigslist o lo o fa’atau ai ticket e mafai ona fa’aaogā e isi mo aso e tele.
eng_text: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: E ui o lenei gaioiga e taatele, ua fa’asaina e le Disney: o ticket e mo na o le tagata e to’atasi.
eng_text: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: So’o se tōlauapiga i lalo ifo o 'augutu o le Grand Canyon e mana’omia lava se pemita mo nu'u i tua.
eng_text: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: E fa’atapula’aina pemita ina ia puipui'a le vanu, ma e avanoa i le aso muamua o le masina, fā masina a'o le i amataina le masina.
eng_text: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: O lea, o le pemita mo nu'u i tua mo so’o se aso lava o Mē e maua i le aso muamua o Ianuari.
eng_text: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: O avanoa mo nofoaga lauiloa, e pei o le Agelu Mālamalamala lea e latalata i le Phantom Ranch, e tele lava ina fa’atumulia i talosaga e maua mai i faigā'uo fa'atoa tafafao fa’atasi ma ua tatalaina mo tafaoga e fa'afeso’otai mai.
eng_text: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: E fa’atapula’aina numera o pemita e fa’aagaga mo tagata e omai i le ofisa ma talosaga ai avanoa, i luga o le fa’avae o le ave o le avanoa i lē muamua mai.
eng_text: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: O le ulufale atu i Aferika i Saute i le taavale o se auala matagofie e matamata ai i le lalelei o itu uma o le atunuu fa’apea ai ma le asiasi atu i nofoaga i ala e ‘ese mai i auala masani o tagata tafafao maimoa.
eng_text: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: E mafai ona faia lenei mea i taavale masani ma fuafuaga fa’aeteete peita’i e fautuaina maualuga le 4x4 ma o le tele o nofoaga e na o le 4x4 uili maualuluga e mafai ona oo iai.
eng_text: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Ia manatua a o faia fuafuaga e ui o Aferika i Saute e malu puipuia ae e le atunuu tuā’oi uma.
eng_text: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: O mea mana’omia i visa ma tau e le tutusa mai lea atunuu i lea atunuu ma e aafia i le atunuu e te sau mai ai.
eng_text: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: O atunuu ta’itasi e iai tulafono fa’apitoa e mana’omia ai le iai o mea e tatau mo fa’alavelave fa’afuase’i i totonu o taavale.
eng_text: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: O Victora Falls o se taulaga i se vaega o le itu i sisifo o Zimbabwe, i le isi itu o le tuā’oi mai Livisitone (Livingstone), Zambia, ma latalata i Botswana.
eng_text: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: O le taulaga e ta’oto tonu lava i tafatafa o afu, ma o ni mata’aga autū, peita’i o lenei nofoaga lauiloa mo turisi e ofoina atu i tagata e fiafia i nofoaga e le i oo muamua iai (adventure seekers) ma tagata matamata le tele o avanoa e nonofo ai i se taimi umi.
eng_text: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: I le vaitau o timuga (Novema ia Mati), o le a siisii le maualuga o le vai ma o le a fa’aeteetegatā foi Afu.
eng_text: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: E mautinoa lou sūsū pe a e kolosi le auala laupapa pe savali i tafāala ta’amilomilo i autafa o afu.
eng_text: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: I le isi itu, ona ua siisii tele le maualuga o le vai o lau vaai i Afu sa’o o le a punitia - e vai uma!
eng_text: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: O le tuugamau o Tutankhamun (KV62). Masalo o KV62 o le tuugamau sili ona lauiloa i tuugamau uma i le Vanu, o le vaaiga na iloaina e Howard Carter i le 1922 o le tino maliu o le tupu la’ititi e toetoe lava ina leai se mea o fa’aleagaina.
eng_text: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Fa’atusa i le tele o isi tuugamau iloga, o le tuugamau o Tutankhamun e tau le āsia, e la’ititi tele ma e tau leai ni tēuga.
eng_text: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: So o se tasi lava e vaai i fa’amaoniga o mea ua fa’aleagaina i le tino maliu (mummy) a o taumafai e ave’ese mai le pusaoti o le a lē fiafia ona e na o le ulu ma tau’au e iloa.
eng_text: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: O ‘oloa taugata o le tuugamau e le o toe iai i totonu, ae ua ave’ese ma tuuina i le falemata’aga o Aikupito i Kairo.
eng_text: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: O tagata asiasi e fa’atulagaina o latou taimi e sili ai ona asiasi i isi nofoaga.
eng_text: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: Phnom Krom, e 12 km i le itu i saute sisifo o Siem Reap. O lenei malumalu i luga o le mauga sa fausia i le fa’ai’uga o le 9 seneturi, i le vaitaimi o le nofoa’iga a le Tupu o Yasovarman.
eng_text: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: O le fa’amalumalu mai o le si’osi’omaga o le malumalu ma le vaaiga i luga atu o le vaituloto o le Tonle Sap ua avea ma se fa’alogona fiafia e a’ea ai le mauga.
eng_text: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: O se matamataga i lea nofoaga e matuā manaia pe a tuu iai ma se folauga i le vaa e asiasi ai i le vaituloto.
eng_text: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: E mana’omia le Angkor Pass e ulufale atu ai i le malumalu, o le mea lea ‘aua ne’i galo ona aumai lou tusifolau pe a e asiasi atu i le Tonle Sap.
eng_text: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: O Ierusalema o le taulaga ma o le aai pito sili ona telē o Isaraelu, e ui ina le iloa e isi atunuu ma Malō Aufa’atasi o se aai o Isaraelu.
eng_text: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: O le aai mai anamuā i Mauga o Iutaia (Judean Hills) e iai lona tala fa’asolopito mata’ina mai le faitau afe o tausaga.
eng_text: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: O le aai e pa’ia i talitonuga fa’ale-lotu e tolu - Fa’a-Iutaia, Kerisiano ma le Isalama, ma o se nofoaga e fa’ale-agaga, fa’ale-lotu, ma fa’ale-aganuu.
eng_text: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Ona o le taūa fa’ale-lotu o le aai, aemaise ai le tele o nofoaga o le Aai Tuai, o Ierusalema o le tasi o nofoaga autū mo turisi i Isaraelu.
eng_text: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: E tele nofoaga o tala’aga o Ierusalema, su’esu’ega o laufanua ma nofoaga fa’ale-aganuu fa’atasi ai ma vavaō, o le tumutumu o fale’oloa tetele fai fa’atau i totonu ole taulaga, o fale kofe ma fale’aiga.
eng_text: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: E mana’omia e Ekuatoa tagatanuu o Cuba ona iai ni latou tusi valaaulia ae le i ulufale i Ekuatoa i malae vaalele fa’a-va-o-malō po o nofoaga e ulufale ai.
eng_text: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: O lenei tusi e tatau ona fa’atulafonoina e le Matagaluega o le Va i Fafo a Ekuatoa, ma tali i mea e mana’omia.
eng_text: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: O nei mea mana’omia ua faia ina ia faamaopoopo lelei femalagaa’iga i le va o atunuu e lua.
eng_text: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: O tagatanuu o Cuba e umia card meamata a le US e tatau ona āsia le Konesula a Ekuatoa e aumai ai se pepa fa’atagaina.
eng_text: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: E tatau ona aogā lou tusifolau mo le 6 masina i tua atu o aso o lau malaga. O se pepa malaga taamilo/fa’aauau e mana’omia e fa’amaonia ai le ‘umi o lau nofo.
eng_text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: E taugofie tafaoga i kulupu tetele, o le mea lea afai na o oe e po o oulua ma se uō, taumafai e vaai nisi tagata ina ia maua ai ni kulupu o ni tagata e to’afa i le to’aono mo se tau lelei.
eng_text: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Peita’i, e le tatau ona e popole i lea mea aua o le tele o taimi e fesuisuia’i ai turisi i le fa’atumuina o taavale.
eng_text: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: E foliga mai o se mea e fa’atogafiti ona fai mo tagata ina ia talitonu ai e tatau ona totogi se tupe e sili atu.
eng_text: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: O le pito i matū o Machu Picchu o lo o fa’amalumalu mai ai i luga le mauga tifatō, e masani ona fai ma ata pito i tua i le tele o ata pu’e o fa’atafunaga.
eng_text: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: E tau foliga taufa’afefe pe a vaai mai i lalo, ma e tifatō ma faigata ona a’ea, ae o tagata e sili ona malolosi e tatau ona mafaia ona a’ea i totonu o le 45 minute.
eng_text: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: O sitepu maa e paepae i luga o le tele o auala, ma e o vaega tifatō o lo o iai uaea u’amea e lagolagoina pito e pipii ai lima.
eng_text: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: I le faiatu ai, ia e nofouta e ono vave ona e tau le mānava, ma e fa’aeteete i vaega tifatō, aemaise lava pe a sūsū, auā e vave ona lē saogalemū.
eng_text: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: E iai se tama’i ana e latalata i le pito i luga e tatau ona pasia, e fai sina maulalo ma pe va itiiti.
eng_text: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: O matamataga i mata’aga ma vaomatua o Galapagos e sili ai le ō i vaa, e pei ona faia e Charles Darwin i le 1835.
eng_text: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: E ova ma le 60 vaa tafafao na fa’atumulia ai le gataifale o Galapagos - amata mai le 8 i le 100 tagata asiasi.
eng_text: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: O le tele o tagata e fa’atonu mamao o latou nofoaga (auā e tele ina tumu le vaa i taimi pisi o le tausaga).
eng_text: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Ia mautinoa o le tagata o lo o fa’atonu ai lou nofoaga o se tagata fa’apitoa o Galapagos e malamalama lelei i le tele o vaa.
eng_text: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: O le mea lea e fa’amautinoa ai o mea e te fiafia iai ma/po o tulaga lē lelei e fetaui ma le vaa e matua’i talafeagai mo latou.
eng_text: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Ae le i taunuu mai le ‘au Sipaniolo i le 16 seneturi, o Chile i matū sa i lalo o pule’aga a Inca a o nofoia ai e tagatanuu moni o Araucanians (Mapuche) le totonugalemū ma saute o Chile.
eng_text: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: O Mapuche o isi foi o fa’apotopotoga tuto’atasi o tagatanuu moni o Amerika, e le i toso tele atu e pule’aga a tagata tautatala i le gagana Sipaniolo seia mae’a le tuto’atasi o Chile.
eng_text: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: E ui lava in tuto’atasi Chile i le 1810 (i le vaitaimi o le taua a Napoleone lea na mafatia ai Spain i le leai o se latou faigamalō lelei mo nai tausaga), o le manumalo a’ia’i ia Spain fa’ato’ā ausia i le 1818.
eng_text: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: O le Malō o Tomenika (Sipaniolo: Malō o Tomenika ) o se atunu’u i le Karipiana o lo'o nofoia le afa i sasa’e o le motu o Isipaniolo, lea e faasoa ma Haiti.
eng_text: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: E ese mai matāfaga ’one’one papa’e, ma laufanua maugā, o le atunuu o le nofoaga e pito sili ona leva i Europa i a'ai o Amerika, lea ua avea nei ma vaega o Santo Domingo.
eng_text: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: O le motu na mu’ai nofoia e Taino ma Karipi. O Karipi o tagata e tautatala i le Gagana Arauaka na taunu'u mai ile 10,000TLM.
eng_text: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: I totonu o ni nai tausaga talu na taunu'u mai tagata sa’ili’ili mai Europa, na mataulia ai le matua’i fa’aiti'itia o le faitau aofa’i o Taino e le 'au Sipaniolo manumalo
eng_text: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Fa’avae i luga o fa’amatalaga a le Faifeau o Felei Patolomaio (Feagaiga ma Initia) i le va o le 1492 ma le 1498 na fasiotia ai e le au Sipaniolo le 100,000 tagata Taino.
eng_text: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Togalaau tuufa’atasi (Jardín de la Unión). O lenei galuega sa fausia mo le nofoaga fa’ale-lotu o le seneturi 17, lea e totoe mai ai na o le fale o le Temple de San Diego.
eng_text: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Ua avea nei ma nofoaga tutotonu mo pisinisi ‘ese’ese, ma e tele lava mea e masani ona tutupu ai, i le ao ma le po.
eng_text: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: E tele fale’aiga e si’osi’oina le togalaau, ma e o aoauli ma afiafi e fai ai koneseti e leai se totogi e masani ona faia mai i le gazebo tutotonu.
eng_text: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Auala vaapiapi o le Kisi). E lua fa’apaologa e va i le na o le 69 senitimita o le fale o se talatuu o le alofa.
eng_text: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Mo ni nai sene e fa’amatalaina atu ai e ni tamaiti le tala ia te oe.
eng_text: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: O le motu o Bowen e lauiloa i malaga o le aso po o malaga pupuu o le fa’ai’uga o le vaiaso e ofaina alogā-vaa, savaliga i luga o mauga, fale’oloa, fale’aiga, ma isi mea.
eng_text: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: O lenei nuu mavae e i Howe Sound i fafo atu a o Vancouver, ma e faigofie ona ulufale iai i taxi vaa e tuua le Motu o Granville i le taulaga o Vancouver.
eng_text: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Mo i latou e fiafia i gaioiga e fai i fafo, e taūa le savaliga i luga o le Sami aga’i auala o le Lagi.
eng_text: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: O Whistler (1.5 itulā e sau ai mai Vancouver i le taavale) e taugatā ae e lauiloa ona o taaloga o le Olimipeka i le Tau malūlū o le 2010.
eng_text: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: I le tau malūlū, fa’afiafia oe i nisi o fa’aseega i luga o le aisa sili ona lelei i Amerika i Matū, ma i le tau mafanafana fa’ata’ita’i i nisi o ti’eti’ega uila moni i luga o mauga.
eng_text: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: E tatau ona fa’atau mamao atu sau pemita. E tatau ona iai sau pemita e te nofo ai i Sirena i le po.
eng_text: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: O Sirena e na o le pau lea o le falenofo o tagata e vaaia mata’aga fa’ale-natura o lo o iai falemau totogi ma mea’ai vevela e fa’aopoopo i tolauapiga. O La Leona, San Pedrillo, ma Los Patos e ofaina tolauapiga e leai ni mea’ai.
eng_text: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: E mafai ona maua lau pemita o le paka e tuusa’o mai le Ranger Station i Puerto Jiménez, ae latou te le taliaina credit cards.
eng_text: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: O ‘Au’aunaga a le Paka (MINAE) e le mafai ona tuuina muamua atu se pemita i le sili atu ma le masina ae le’i taunuu mai.
eng_text: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: E ofaina atu e le CafeNet El Sol ‘au’aunaga e taofi ai avanoa i le tau e $30 Amerika po o le $10 mo le pasi i le aso e tasi; o fa’amatalaga o lo o i le itulau a le Corcovado.
eng_text: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: O le Atu Kuki o ni motu e iai sootaga sa’oloto ma Ni’u Sila, e i le Polenisia i le ogatotonu o le Vasa Pasefika i Saute.
eng_text: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: O se atumotu e 15 motu e tūtū solo i totonu o le 2.2 miliona km2 o le vasa.
eng_text: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: Ona o le tutusa o sone o taimi ma Hawaii, o nisi taimi e manatu ai o se “motu i lalo o Hawaii.”
eng_text: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: E ui ina la’ititi, o se fa’amanatu i nisi o tagata asiasi matutua o Hawaii ae le i avea ma setete e leai ni faletalimalō tetele mo turisi ma isi atina’e.
eng_text: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: O le Atu Kuki e leai ni taulaga ae e fausiaina e motu ‘ese’ese e 15. O motu autū o Rarotonga ma Aitutaki.
eng_text: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: I atunuu atina’e i aso nei, o le sauniaina o moega i tulaga maualuga ma ti o le taeao ua siitia i se tulaga o ata-fa’atulagaina.
eng_text: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: I le pito i luga, e manino ai le tauva o le B&Bs i vaega autū e lua: o moega ma le ti o le taeao.
eng_text: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: E tusa ai ma tulaga lelei o atina’ega, o totonu o nei fale e mafai e se tasi ona su’eina le moega i lona tulaga sili ona matagofie, a le o se ie teuteu sa su’i lima po o se moega ua tausagā.
eng_text: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: O ti o le taeao e ono maua ai ni mea’ai o le vaitau o lo o ua iai po o le taumafataga fa’apitoa a le talimalō.
eng_text: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: O le tulaga, o se fale tuai mai aso anamua e aofia ai meāfale ua tausagā, laufaunua māmā ma se vaita’ele.
eng_text: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: O le oso i totonu o le taavale ma alu i se malaga umi i luga o le ala e iai le fa’alogona fiafia i le matagofie.
eng_text: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: E le pei o taavale tetele, masalo ua e masani i le aveina o lau taavale ma iloa ona limiti.
eng_text: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: O le fa’atuina o se fale’ie i luga o meatotino tuma’oti po o le taulaga i so o se ituaiga, e faigofie ona tosina atu iai tagata e le mana’omia.
eng_text: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: I le fa’apuupuuga, o le fa’aaogāina o lau taavale o se auala e sili atu e alu ai le malaga i le ala ae seāseā ona fa’aaogā i se “tolauapiga”.
eng_text: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: O taavale mo tolauapiga e talafeagai pe afai e iai sau minivan telē, SUV, Sedan po o le Station Wagon e iai nofoa e mafai ona fa’amomoe i lalo.
eng_text: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: O nisi faletalimalō e iai tamaoaiga maua mai i le tausaga auro o nofoaafi e ola i le ausa vevela ma vaa la’upasese tetele; i luma mai o le Taua lona Lua a le Lalolagi, i le seneturi 19 po o le amataga o le 20 seneturi.
eng_text: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: O nei faletalimalō sa nonofo ai le au mau’oa ma le tagata ta’uta’ua o le aso, ma e tele ona fai taumafataga lelei ma fiafia i evaga o le po.
eng_text: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: O teuga tuai, o le lē lava o meāfale fou, ma se tulaga mautinoa o le matua, o vaega foi ia o le latou tino mai.
eng_text: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: E ui ina masani o ni meatotino ma’oti, o nisi taimi latou te fa’afaleina ai ao o le malō asiasi atu ma isi tagata mamalu o le malō.
eng_text: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: O se tagata malaga ma ana fa’aputugatupe e tatau ona ia mafaufau e malaga taamilo i le lalolagi i se vaalele, fa’amotuina ai le nofo i le tele o nei faletalimalō.
eng_text: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: O se sootaga fesuia’i o tagata talimalō o se fa’apotopotoga latou te fesoota’ia tagata malaga ma tagatanuu i totonu o taulaga o le a asiasi iai.
eng_text: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: O le auai ai i lea fa’apotopotoga e masani ona mana’omia na o le fa’atumuina o se pepa fa’atumu i luga o ‘upega tafa’ilagi; e ui lava o nisi fa’apotopotoga e saunia po o le mana’omia o pepa fa’amaonia fa’aopoopo.
eng_text: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: O le lisi o tagata talimalō e sauniaina, a le lolomiina ma/po o le ‘upega tafa’ilagi, o nisi taimi o pepa fa’amaonia ma iloiloga mai isi tagata malaga.
eng_text: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: O le couchsurfing na fa’avaeina ia Ianuari 2004 ina ua maua e le ali’i polokalama komepiuta o Casey Fenton se malaga taugofie i Iceland ae leai se mea e nofo ai.
eng_text: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: Na ia imeli i tamaiti a’oga i le Iunivesite o le lotoifale ma ia maua ai le tele o ofa mo le nofo fua ai.
eng_text: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: O nofotumau latou te fa’amuamuaina le tupulaga talavou - o se malō masani e luasefulu tausaga - ae e masani foi ona maua iai tagata malaga matutua.
eng_text: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: O aiga ma tamaiti e seāseā vaaia, ae o nisi nofotumau latou te taliaina i latou i potu fa’apitoa.
eng_text: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: O le aai o Beijing i Saina o le a talimalō i Taaloga Olimipeka o le Taumalūlū i le 2022, ma o le a avea ai ma taulaga muamua ua talimalō i taaloga uma o le Olimipeka o le tau mafanafana ma le tau malūlū.
eng_text: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

text: O le a talimalō Beijing i le tatalaina ma sauniga tapuniina ma taaloga i totonu i luga o le aisa.
eng_text: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

text: O isi taaloga fa’asee i le aisa o le a faia i le malae fa’asee i Taizicheng i Zhangjiakou, pe tusa ma le 220 km (140 maila) mai Beijing.
eng_text: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

text: O le tele o malumalu e fai a latou fa’afiafiaga Fa’ale-tausaga e amata mai ia Novema ae fa’ai’u i le ogatotonu o Me, ma e ‘ese’ese lava auā e fua i kalena fa’ale-tausaga a malumalu ta’itasi.
eng_text: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

text: O le tele o fa’afiafiaga a malumalu e fa’amanatu o se vaega o le atoaga o tausaga o le malumalu po o le asofanau o le atua po o se isi fa’amanatuga fa’apitoa e fesoota’i ma le malumalu.
eng_text: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

text: O fa’afiafiaga o malumalu a Kerala e manaia tele i le matamata, o a latou elefane ua teuteuina i teuga masani, faa’ili a le malumalu ma isi mea fa’afiafia.
eng_text: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

text: O Fa’aaliga a le Lalolagi (e iloa tele i le World Exposition, po o le Expo) o le vaega pito sili ona telē i le fa’alauiloaina fa’a-va-o-malō o fa’afiafiaga fa’atufugaga ma fa’asaienisi.
eng_text: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

text: O atunuu auai e fa’aalia ata tusi ma fa’aaliga fa’ale-a’oa’oga i fale o le malō e fa’aalia ai fa’afitauli o le lalolagi po o aganuu ma tala fa’asolopito a o latou atunuu.
eng_text: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

text: O Fa’aaliga o Mea Tōtō Fa’a-va-o-malō o fa’alauiloa fa’apitoa e fa’aalia ai fugalaau, togalaau ma so o se mea tau laau.
eng_text: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

text: E ui i fa’amaumauga e mafai ona fai i tausaga uma (se’i vagana ua ‘ese’ese atunuu), o le mea moni, e le o faia.
eng_text: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

text: O nei fa’aaliga e masani ona uma i se mea o le va o le tolu masina ma le ono masina, ma e faia i nofoaga e le la’ititi ifo ma le 50 eka.
eng_text: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

text: E tele ituaiga o ata ‘ese’ese sa fa’aaogāina i le tele o tausaga. O ata tifaga masani 35 mm (36 i le 24 mm negative) e sili ona taatele.
eng_text: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

text: E tele ina faigofie ona toe fa’atumuina pe a uma, ma aumai ai ma ituaiga o ata fa’atusatusa i le DSLR i le taimi nei.
eng_text: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

text: O isi meapu’e ata e fa’aaogāina le ituaiga o le 6 i le 6 cm, e sili atu le manino o le 56 i le 56 mm negative.
eng_text: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

text: O le mea lea e sau ai le resolution e toeititi fa’afaina le 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 fa’atusa i le 864).
eng_text: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

text: O le olaga i le vao e i totonu o lu’itau sili o fa’ailoilo mo tagata pu’eata, ma e mana’omia tuufa’atasiga o fa’amanuiaga, onosa’i, poto masani ma meafaigaluega lelei.
eng_text: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

text: O ata pu’e o le olaga i le vao e masani ona manatu fa’atauvaa iai, ae o ata pu’e i so o se mea, o se ata e tasi ua tusa ma le afe o upu.
eng_text: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

text: O ata pu’e i le vao e tele ina mana’omia ai se tioata umī, o isi mea e pei o se lafu manulele po o se manu la’ititi e mana’omia isi tioata.
eng_text: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

text: O le tele o manu mai fafo e faigata ona su’e, ma o paka o isi taimi e iai tulafono i le pu’eina o ata mo mafua’aga tau pisinisi.
eng_text: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

text: O manufe’ai e iai taimi e fa’amananaia ai po o le ulavavale. O le si’osi’omaga e ono malūlū, vevela, po o le paū.
eng_text: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

text: E ova ma le 5,000 gagana ‘ese’ese i le lalolagi, e aofia ai le silia ma le luasefulu ma le 50 miliona po o le tele o tagata tautatala i gagana.
eng_text: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

text: O le gagana tusitusi e faigofie ona malamalama na i lo le gagana tautala. E matua’i sa’o lava lenei mea i tuātusi, lea e masani e faigata ona fa’aleo ia sa’o.
eng_text: Written words are often easier to understand than spoken words, also. This is especially true of addresses, which are often difficult to pronounce intelligibly.

text: E tele atunuu e malamalama lelei i le Igilisi, ma sili atu ae e te ono maua ai ni tagata e utiuti le iloa - aemaise lava i tupulaga laiti.
eng_text: Many entire nations are completely fluent in English, and in even more you can expect a limited knowledge - especially among younger people.

text: Mafaufau iai, afai e te mafai, o se tagata mai Manchester, o Boston, Jamaica ma Sini e nonofo fa’ataamilo i se laulau’ai o lo o fai se latou taumafataga i se fale’aiga i Toronto.
eng_text: Imagine, if you will, a Mancunian, Bostonian, Jamaican and Sydneysider sitting around a table having dinner at a restaurant in Toronto.

text: O lo o fa’amatala fiafia a latou tala i o latou nuu, i akasegi ‘ese’ese ma la latou lava gagana.
eng_text: They're regaling each other with stories from their hometowns, told in their distinct accents and local argot.

text: O le fa’atauina o meaai i le supamaketi e masani o se auala taugofie e aai ai. A leai se iloa i mea tau kuka, o filifiliga i meaai fai i le fale e limiti.
eng_text: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food.

text: Ua fa’ateleina mea’ai kuka ‘ese’ese i vaega o mea’ai i supamaketi. O nisi latou te saunia ogaumu microwave po o isi mea e fa’avevela ai mea’ai.
eng_text: Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food.

text: I nisi atunuu po o ituaiga o fale’oloa e iai lava le fale’aiga i le itu, e masani o se fale’aiga la’ititi taugofie.
eng_text: In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

text: Fai ma ave ni kopi o aiaiga ma fa’amatalaga fesoota’i o lau inisiua.
eng_text: Make and carry copies of your policy and your insurer's contact details with you.

text: E mana’omia le fa’aali o le imeli a lau inisiua ma le telefoni fa’a-va-o-malō mo fautuaga/fa’atagana ma le faiga o tagi.
eng_text: They need to show the insurer's e-mail address and international phone numbers for advice/authorizations and making claims.

text: Tuu se isi kopi i lau ‘ato ma luga o le initaneti (imeli iā te oe le faila, pe sefe i luga o “ao”).
eng_text: Have another copy in your luggage and online (e-mail to yourself with attachment, or stored in the "cloud").

text: A e malaga ma se komepiuta po o se tapeleti, sefe se kopi i le memory po o se disc (e mafai ona tatalaina e aunoa ma le initaneti).
eng_text: If traveling with a laptop or tablet, store a copy in its memory or disc (accessible without the internet).

text: Ave foi kopi o aiaiga ma fesoota’iga i tagata o la outou malaga ma aiga po o uō i lou atunuu o lo o fia fesoasoani.
eng_text: Also give policy/contact copies to traveling companions and relatives or friends back home willing to help.

text: O musi (lea e iloa foi o le elk) e le ulavavale tele, ae latou te puipuia latou lava pe a iai se lapata’iga.
eng_text: Moose (also known as elk) aren't inherently aggressive, but will defend themselves if they perceive a threat.

text: E le iloa e tagata o musi e iai taimi e leaga ai, o lo latou fa’alatalata iai e ona tuuina ai i latou ini fa’alavelave.
eng_text: When people don't see moose as potentially dangerous, they may approach too closely and put themselves at risk.

text: O le inu ‘ava malosi ma le fa’aeteete. O le ‘ava malosi e ‘ese’ese ona aafiaga i tagata, ma o le iloa o ou limiti e taūa tele.
eng_text: Drink alcoholic drinks with moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, and knowing your limit is very important.

text: O aafiaga ‘umi o le tagofia tele o le ‘ava malosi e mafai ona fa’aleagaina ai le ate ma e oo foi ina tauaso ai le vaai ma maliu ai. O lona leaga e fa’ateteleina ina ua tagofia ‘ava malosi le fa’atulafonoina.
eng_text: Possible long term health events from excessive drinking can include liver damage and even blindness and death. The potential danger is increased when consuming illegally produced alcohol.

text: O ‘ava malosi lē fa’atulafonoina e ona maua iai le tele o mea e ono lamatia ai le soifua malōlōina e iai le methanol, lea e ono mafua ai le pō o le vaai po o le oti tusa lava pe o ni nai fa’atulutulu.
eng_text: Illegal spirits can contain various dangerous impurities including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small doses.

text: O mata tioata e ono taugofie i atunuu i fafo aemaise ai atunuu e pa’ū maualalo latou tupe maua ma maualalo totogi o galuega.
eng_text: Eyeglasses can be cheaper in a foreign country, especially in low-income countries where labour costs are lower.

text: Mafaufau e fai se siaki o ou mata i le fale, aemaise lava pe afai o lo o kavaina e le inisiua, ma aumai le pepa o fa’amatalaga ina ia failaina i se isi mea.
eng_text: Consider getting an eye exam at home, especially if insurance covers it, and bringing the prescription along to be filed elsewhere.

text: O fa’avaa taugata e maua i ia ituaiga o nofoaga e ono iai fa’afitauli e lua; o nisi o ni kopi, ae o mea moni e fa’atau mai i fafo e ono sili atu le taugata na i lo i lou atunuu.
eng_text: High-end brand-name frames available in such areas may have two problems; some may be knock-offs, and the real imported ones may be more expensive than at home.

text: O le kofe o se tasi o ‘oloa e sili ona fa’atauina i le lalolagi, ma e masalo e te ono mauaina le tele o ituaiga ‘ese’ese i lou atunuu.
eng_text: Coffee is one of the world's most traded commodities, and you can probably find many types in your home region.

text: Ae peita’i, e tele auala ‘ese’ese o le inuina o le kofe i le lalolagi e tatau ona asiasi iai e molimauina.
eng_text: Nevertheless, there are many distinctive ways of drinking coffee around the world that are worth experiencing.

text: O le canyoning (po o le: canyoneering) e fa’atatau i le alu i le ta’ēle o le vanu, lea a le mago po o le tumu i vai.
eng_text: Canyoning (or: canyoneering) is about going in a bottom of a canyon, which is either dry or full of water.

text: O le taaloga o le canyoning e tuufa’atasia elemeni mai le ‘a’au, a’e ma le oso--ae mana’omia nai toleniga po o le lelei o le tino mo le amataina (fa’atusaina i a’ega mauga, moulu i lalo o le sami po o le fa’asee i luga o mauga, mo le fa’ata’ita’iga).
eng_text: Canyoning combines elements from swimming, climbing and jumping--but requires relatively little training or physical shape to get started (compared to rock climbing, scuba diving or alpine skiing, for example).

text: O savaliga o se gaioiga e fai i fafo e aofia ai le savavali i si’osi’omaga fa’alenatura, e masani o luga o ni auala savavali.
eng_text: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often on hiking trails.

text: O savaliga e aofia ai le mamao e la’ititi ifo i le maila e oo atu i mamao ‘umi lea e mafai ona kava i le aso e tasi.
eng_text: Day hiking involves distances of less than a mile up to longer distances that can be covered in a single day.

text: Mo se savaliga i le aso i luga o se auala faigofie, e mana’omia tapenaga laiti, ma o so o se tagata malosi lava e fiafia iai.
eng_text: For a day hike along an easy trail little preparations are needed, and any moderately fit person can enjoy them.

text: O aiga e iai tamaiti laiti e ono mana’omia le tele o tapenapenaga, ae o se aso i fafo e faigofie lava e oo i pepe ma tamaiti a’oga fa’ata’ita’i.
eng_text: Families with small children may need more preparations, but a day outdoors is easily possible even with babies and pre-school children.

text: Fa’a-va-o-malō, e latalata i le 200 fa’apotopotoga o matamataga tamomo’e. O le tele e galulue tuto’atasi.
eng_text: Internationally, there are nearly 200 running tour organizations. Most of them operate independently.

text: O tagata muamua na amataina le Global Running Tours, o le Go Running Tours na fesoota’iina le to’atele o tagata e saunia tamo’ega matamata i le fa konetineta.
eng_text: The Global Running Tours successor, Go Running Tours networks dozens of sightrunning providers on four continents.

text: I le iai o tupu’aga i Paselona o Matamataga Tamomo’e i Paselona ma Tamo’ega i Copenhagen, sa vave ona auai atu iai Matamataga Tamomo’e i Prague i totonu o Prague ma isi.
eng_text: With roots in Barcelona's Running Tours Barcelona and Copenhagen's Running Copenhagen, it was quickly joined by Running Tours Prague based in Prague and others.

text: E tele mea e tatau ona e mafaufau iai muamua ae e te le i malaga ma le taimi ua e malaga ai i se isi nofoaga.
eng_text: There are many things you have to take into consideration before and when you travel somewhere.

text: A e malaga ‘aua ne’i e mafaufau e tutusa mea uma ma mea e faia i “lou aiga”. O tu ma aga, tulafono, mea’ai, pisi o auala, tulaga o mea e nonofo ai, gagana ma isi mea e iai ni mea e ‘ese’ese ai mai le mea e te nofo ai.
eng_text: When you travel, expect things not to be like they are "back home". Manners, laws, food, traffic, lodging, standards, language and so on will to some extent differ from where you live.

text: O le mea lenei o se mea e tatau lava ona teu i le mafaufau, ina ia ‘alofia le fa’anoanoa po o le lē fiafia i auala fa’alotoifale e faia ai mea.
eng_text: This is something you always need to keep in mind, to avoid disappointment or perhaps even distaste over local ways to do things.

text: O ofisa malaga ua leva ona iai talu mai le 19 seneturi. O se ofisa malaga e masani o se filifiliga lelei mo se faigamalaga e fa’alautele ai le agavaa o le tagata malaga i le natura, aganuu, gagana po o atunuu e laiti tupe maua.
eng_text: Travel agencies have been around since the 19th century. A travel agent is usually a good option for a journey which extends beyond a traveller's previous experience of nature, culture, language or low-income countries.

text: E ui o le tele o ofisa malaga e malilie e talia le taofiga masani o avanoa, o le tele o ofisa fa’apitoa mo ituaiga o malaga, fa’asoasoaina o le paketi po o le nofoaga autū e taunuu iai.
eng_text: Although most agencies are willing to take on most regular bookings, many agents specialise in particular types of travel, budget ranges or destinations.

text: E sili atu le fa’aaogā o se ofisa malaga e masani ona faia malaga e tutusa ma lau malaga.
eng_text: It can be better to use an agent who frequently books similar trips to yours.

text: Vaavaai po o a malaga o lo o fa’alauiloaina e le ofisa malaga, a le o le ‘upega tafa’ilagi po o totonu i se fa’amalama o se fale’oloa.
eng_text: Take a look at what trips the agent is promoting, whether on a website or in a shop window.

text: A e fia matamata i le lalolagi i se tau taugofie, mo mea mana’omia, olaga lelei po o lu’itau, e iai auala e fai ai.
eng_text: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that.

text: O le mea moni, e pa’ū i vaega e lua: A lē faigaluega a’o e malaga po o le taumafai e limiti au tupe fa’aalu. O lenei tusitusiga e taula’i i le mea mulimuli.
eng_text: Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter.

text: Mo ē ua malilie e ofa atu fa’amāmā avega, taimi ma le mafaufau e ūna’ia ai i lalo le tupe fa’aalu ia latalata i le zero, vaai le paketi la’ititi mo malaga.
eng_text: For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel.

text: O fautuaga ua fa’ailoa ai o tagata faimalaga e le gaoi, solitofaga, auai i vaega o maketi fa’asolitulafono, aisi, po o le fa’aaogā o isi tagata mo lo latou lelei.
eng_text: The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.

text: O le taofiga muamua lava o le ofisa o femalagaa’iga ina ua o ‘ese mai le vaalele, o se vaa, po o se isi taavale.
eng_text: An immigration checkpoint is usually the first stop when disembarking from a plane, a ship, or another vehicle.

text: I nisi o nofoaafi e kolosiina tuā’oi o asiasiga e faia a o alu le nofoaafi ma e tatau ona iai lou ID o aogā pea ia oe ina ua e oso i totonu o se tasi o nei noafoaafi.
eng_text: In some cross-border trains inspections are done on the running train and you should have valid ID with you when boarding one of those trains.

text: I po o e momoe ai nofoaafi, e ono aoina tusifolau e le ta’ita’i ina ia ‘aua ne’i fa’alavelaveina lau moe.
eng_text: On night sleeper trains, passports may be collected by the conductor so that you do not have your sleep interrupted.

text: O le lesitala o se vaega fa’aopoopo o mea mana’omia mo le fa’agaioiga o le visa. I nisi o atunuu, e tatau ona lesitala lou nofo ai ma le tuātusi o le mea o lo o e nofo ai i pulega o le lotoifale.
eng_text: Registration is an additional requirement for the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and address where you are staying with the local authorities.

text: O le mea lenei e ono mana’omia ai le fa’atumuina o le pepa fa’atumu i le ofisa o leoleo o le lotoifale po o le asiasi i le ofisa o femalagaa’iga.
eng_text: This might require filling out a form with the local police or a visit to the immigration offices.

text: I le tele o atunuu e iai ia tulafono, o faletalimalō o le a latou taulimaina le faiga o lesitala (ia mautinoa le fesili).
eng_text: In many countries with such a law, local hotels will handle the registration (make sure to ask).

text: I isi taimi, na o ē e nonofo ‘ese mai ma faletalimalō mo turisi e mana’omia le lesitala. Peita’i, o le mea lea ua atili ai ona fa’afaigata, su’esu’e ae le i malaga ‘ese.
eng_text: In other cases, only those staying outside of tourist accommodations need to register.  However, this makes the law much more obscure, so find out beforehand.

text: O ata fa’akamuta e fa’atatau i le mamanuina ma le fausiaina o fale. O le fausaga o se nofoaga e masani o se mata’aga mo turisi i lona ia tulaga.
eng_text: Architecture is concerned with the design and construction of buildings. The architecture of a place is often a tourist attraction in its own right.

text: O le tele o fale e matagofie le tilotilo atu iai, ma le vaaiga mai se fale maualuga pe mai se fa’amalama e atamai le fa’atulagaina e mafai ona avea m se vaaiga aulelei e taofi iai.
eng_text: Many buildings are quite beautiful to look at and the view from a tall building or from a cleverly-positioned window can be a beauty to behold.

text: Ua fefiloi ata fa’akamuta ma isi ata e iai le fuafuaga o le taulaga, inisinia sivili, ata teuteu, mamanu mo totonu ma le fa’ataatiaga o laufanua.
eng_text: Architecture overlaps considerably with other fields including urban planning, civil engineering, decorative arts, interior design and landscape design.

text: E tusa ai ma le mamao o le tele o nuu, e te le maua se taimi telē mo tafaoga i le po e aunoa ma lou malaga i Albuquerque po o Santa Fe.
eng_text: Given how remote many of the pueblos are, you won't be able to find a significant amount of nightlife without traveling to Albuquerque or Santa Fe.

text: Ae peita’i, o le tele o kasino o lo o lisiina latou te fa’ataua vaiinu, ma le to’atele o i latou e aumaia fa’afiafiaga iloga (e muamua lava vaega tetele e si’omiaina le Albuquerque ma Santa Fe).
eng_text: However, nearly all of the casinos listed above serve drinks, and several of them bring in name-brand entertainment (primarily the large ones immediately surrounding Albuquerque and Santa Fe).

text: Fa’aeteete: o pa laiti i le taulaga iinei e le o taimi uma e lelei ai mo tafaoga a tagata asiasi mai i isi nofoaga.
eng_text: Beware: small-town bars here are not always good places for the out-of-state visitor to hang out.

text: O se tasi o mea, o New Mexico i matū e iai ona fa’afitauli fa’apitoa i ave taavale onānā, ma le malosi o le fa’asuā’avā o ave taavale e latalata i le maualuga o ‘ava malosi i pa laiti i le taulaga.
eng_text: For one thing, northern New Mexico has significant problems with drunk driving, and the concentration of intoxicated drivers is high close to small-town bars.

text: O ata (murals) le mana’omia po o ‘osi’osiga e ta’ua o graffiti.
eng_text: Unwanted murals or scribble is known as graffiti.

text: E ui i le mamao ma mea fa’aonaponei, o le tele o tagata masalo e auai fa’atasi ma le tupulaga i le fa’aleagaina o meatotino a le malō ma mea patino a tagata i le tafanaina i vali.
eng_text: While it's far from a modern phenomenon, most people probably associate it with youth vandalizing public and private property using spray paint.

text: Peita’i, o aso nei ua iai tusiata o ituaiga ata ‘ese’ese i luga o pa puipui, o fa’aaliga o ata ma pa puipui “fa’ale-tulafono”. O valigā ata i lea ituaiga e masani ona tutusa galuega na i lo ata nenefu.
eng_text: However, nowadays there are established graffiti artists, graffiti events and "legal" walls. Graffiti paintings in this context often resemble artworks rather than illegible tags.

text: O le togiina o le boomerang o se tomai lauiloa e tele turisi e fia mauaina.
eng_text: Boomerang throwing is a popular skill that many tourists want to acquire.

text: Afai e te mana’o e a’oa’oina le togiina o le boomerang e toe foi mai i lou lima, ia mautinoa e iai se boomerang talafeagai e toe foi mai.
eng_text: If you want to learn throwing a boomerang that comes back to your hand, make sure you have a suitable boomerang for returning.

text: O le tele o boomerang e maua i Ausetalia o le mea moni e le toe-foi mai. O le mea e sili mo tagata fa’atō’a amata ona ‘aua ne’i fa’ata’ita’iina i le savili.
eng_text: Most boomerangs available in Australia are in fact non-returning. It is best for beginners to not try throwing in windy

text: O se Mea’ai Tao e fa’avela i se lua aasa i le ‘ele’ele.
eng_text: A Hangi Meal is cooked in a hot pit in the ground.

text: O le lua a le fa’avevela i maa aasa mai le afi, po o le vevela mai i vaivela fa’anatura ia e matua’i vevela ai le ‘ele’ele i nisi o nofoaga.
eng_text: The pit is either heated with hot stones from a fire, or in some places geothermal heat makes areas of ground naturally hot.

text: O le umu (hangi) e masani ona kuka ai se mea’ai e fa’avelaina i se sitaili manaia.
eng_text: The hangi is often used to cook a traditional roast style dinner.

text: O le tele o vaega o Rotorua e fai ai mea’ai i vaivevela e puna mai i laufanua ae o isi mea’ai e mafai ona fa’ata’ita’iina i Kalaisetete, Ueligitone ma isi nofoaga.
eng_text: Several places in Rotorua offer geothermal hangi, while other hangi can be sampled in Christchurch, Wellington and elsewhere.

text: E lua vasega o le MetroRail i nofoaafi e fela’uina tagata i totonu ma vaega uma o Cape Town: o le MetroPlus (e ta’ua foi o le Vasega Muamua) ma le Metro (e ta’ua o le Vasega Tolu).
eng_text: MetroRail has two classes on commuter trains in and around Cape Town: MetroPlus (also called First Class) and Metro (called Third Class).

text: E manaia atu le MetroPlus ma to’agaogao ae fai lava sina taugatā, peita’i o lo o taugofie lava na i lo ticket masani o metro i Europa.
eng_text: MetroPlus is more comfortable and less crowded but slightly more expensive, though still cheaper than normal metro tickets in Europe.

text: O nofoaafi uma e iai le MetroPlus ma tagata e fa’atonutonuina le Metro; o tagata fa’atonutonu o le MetroPlus e masani lava ona i le fa’atausi’usi’uga o le nofoaafi latalata i le Cape Town.
eng_text: Every train has both MetroPlus and Metro coaches; the MetroPlus coaches are always on the end of the train nearest Cape Town.

text: O lou avea o ato a isi - ‘Aua ne’i ave’esea au ‘ato ma oe, aemaise pe a e kolosiina tuā’oi fa’a-va-o-malō.
eng_text: Carrying for others - Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.

text: E ono mafai ona avea oe ma tagata ave fualaau fa’asāina e aunoa ma sou iloa, ma o le a e aafia ai i fa’afitauli tugā.
eng_text: You could find yourself being used as a drug carrier without your knowledge, which will land you in a great deal of trouble.

text: O lenei mea e aofia ai le fa’atalitali i laina, auā e mafai ona fa’aaogā ta’ifau sosogi i fualaau fa’asāina i so o se taimi e aunoa ma se fa’asilasilaga.
eng_text: This includes waiting in line, as drug-sniffing dogs could be used at any time without notice.

text: O isi atunuu e matuā ogaoga a latou fa’asalaga e oo lava i tagata fa’ato’ā molia muamua; e iai fa’asalaga fa’afalepuipui e mafai ona silia ma le 10 tausaga po o le fa’asala oti.
eng_text: Some countries have exceedingly draconian punishments even for first time offenses; these can include prison sentences of over 10 years or death.

text: O ‘ato fa’ataatitia solo e mata iai tagata gaoi ma e mafai foi ona taula’i iai le vaai a le pulega ina ia mataala mo ni pomu taufa’amata’u.
eng_text: Unattended bags are a target for theft and can also attract attention from authorities wary of bomb threats.

text: I le fale, ona o lou feagai ai pea ma siama i taimi uma, e maualuga le tulaga ua leva ona tatau ona puipuia oe mai nei siama.
eng_text: At home, due to this constant exposure to the local germs, odds are very high that you're already immune to them.

text: Ae o isi itu o le lalolagi e iai nofoaga o siama e fou ia te oe, e mautinoa lava lou aafia i se fa’afitauli.
eng_text: But in other parts of the world, where the bacteriological fauna are new to you, you're far more likely to run into problems.

text: E le gata i lea, o siama e vave fa’ateteleina i tau mafanafana ma umi ona ola i fafo o le tino.
eng_text: Also, in warmer climates bacteria both grow more quickly and survive longer outside the body.

text: O le mea lea o sasa o Delhi Belly, o mala o Farao, o le Taui masui o Montezuma, ma le tele o latou uō.
eng_text: Thus the scourges of Delhi Belly, the Pharaoh's Curse, Montezuma's Revenge, and their many friends.

text: O fa’afitauli i le mānava i tau malūlū, o ma’i tau manava i tau mafanafana e fai lava sina taatele ma o le tele o taimi e fa’amamafa i le mafaufau ae le o se mea e popole tele ai.
eng_text: As with respiratory problems in colder climates, intestinal problems in hot climates are fairly common and in most cases are distinctly annoying but not really dangerous.

text: Afai e te malaga i se atunuu tau atia’e mo le taimi muamua - po o se atunuu fou i le lalolagi - ‘aua ne’i e manatu fa’atauvaa aua e ono fa’ate’ia oe i aganuu a ia nofoaga.
eng_text: If traveling in a developing country for the first time – or in a new part of the world – don't underestimate the potential culture shock.

text: E to’atele e malaga tumau, o tagata e mafai ona malaga e fa’ate’ia i vaaiga fou i atina’ega a le lalolagi o femalagaa’iga, lea ua tele aganuu laiti e mafai ona vave fa’aopoopo iai.
eng_text: Many a stable, capable traveler has been overcome by the newness of developing world travel, where many little cultural adjustments can add up quickly.

text: Aemaise lava i ou aso muamua, mafaufau e fa’aalu au tupe i teuga mai Sisifo ma faletalimalō lelei, meaai, ma ‘au’aunaga ina ia e fa’amasani i ai.
eng_text: Especially in your initial days, consider splurging on Western-style and -quality hotels, food, and services to help acclimatize.

text: ‘Aua e te moe i se fala po o se momi i luga o vao i se nofoaga e te le malamalama i le fanua.
eng_text: Do not sleep on a mattress or pad on the ground in areas where you do not know the local fauna.

text: Afai e te tolauapi i se nofoaga i fafo, ave sau fale mo tolauapiga po o sau taupega ina ia puipuia ai oe mai gata, atalava ma isi manu fa’apena.
eng_text: If you are going to camp out, bring a camp cot or hammock to keep you away from snakes, scorpions and such.

text: Fa’amanogi lou fale i sau kofe aulelei i le taeao ma taumafa sau ti chamomile i le po mo au malologa.
eng_text: Fill your home with a rich coffee in the morning and some relaxing chamomile tea at night.

text: A e nofo i se fale tafao, ua e maua se taimi mo oe ma fa’aaogā ni nai minute e te faia ai se mea lelei mo oe.
eng_text: When you're on a staycation, you have the time to treat yourself and take a few extra minutes to brew up something special.
